#826. Newcastle unrest grows as Barry and Everton give Jaissle another headache

Jack Grealish will do well to get back into the Everton starting lineup when he returns to the squad – as David Moyes’s side are doing just fine without him.

Newcastle were condemned to a second defeat in five days by Moyes’s young team, with a second-half goal from Thierno Barry giving Everton victory against 10 men at St James’ Park after the substitute Jacob Ramsey’s late red card.

And there are still more questions than answers about Matthias Jaissle’s new-look side following a summer of transition at the club, and supporters again voiced their disapproval at the end of the game.

Moyes was reluctant to talk about Grealish’s situation, stating simply that the winger was “unavailable” for a second successive game following a breach of club discipline. But, pressed if there was a way back for the winger, he added: “Of course there is.”

Asked about the resilience of his youthful team, Moyes added: “They’re so good, they give everything they’ve got. They’re a brilliant group of players. We beat Newcastle on Thursday night, and to beat them again today, it’s not an easy thing to do for any club.”

Jaissle acknowledged the reaction of Newcastle supporters to the performance and the result. “Big frustration, big disappointment,” he said. “Of course, the fans, they get frustrated like we are. We need to analyse it now in detail. It’s also clear that I have the responsibility, and I also take that as manager of this club. We need to do things better.”

Newcastle fans had made their feelings about the 3-1 Carabao Cup defeat away to Everton last Thursday clear to Jaissle, who has found himself under pressure early in his tenure. By the time he had gone on to the pitch at Hill Dickinson Stadium to acknowledge their backing, most of the 7,732 travelling supporters had headed for the exits, and St James’ Park emptied just as quickly after the home loss.

Eddie Howe was always going to be a hard act to follow given what he achieved in his first four years as head coach at St James’ Park, but the summer departures of big-name players, and his own 11th-hour arrival, has made the job even harder for Jaissle.

Frustration bubbled away beneath the surface at St James’ Park, a stadium which can be a cauldron when fans are given something to shout about. But the decibel levels were rarely raised in the first period. Newcastle’s Harvey Barnes cut inside late in the half, and an awkward deflection off Jarrad Branthwaite momentarily had Jordan Pickford worried, but, in truth, neither he nor Lukas Hornicek in the home goal were troubled in the first 45 minutes. Jake O’Brien and Harrison Armstrong had chances for Everton late in the half, but both shot wide.

Hornicek, however, was finally tested early in the second half – and a mistake from him handed Barry a goal. The goalkeeper let a shot from the left from Tyrique George squirm under his body, and Barry gratefully tapped the ball into an empty net.

Newcastle have given a number of soft goals away this season, and Jaissle conceded that his team had been caught “sleeping” by Everton, who pressed for a second goal before Yoane Wissa and Sean Steur were sent on by Jaissle.

Steur, after a hugely promising start to life at St James’ Park, has found himself on the bench in recent games to the bemusement of some supporters given how well he performed early in the season following his move from Ajax. Soon after Steur’s introduction, Barnes delivered a ball from the left which was met by Anthony Elanga at the back post. The ball rolled along the line, but did not fully cross it, and Everton cleared the danger.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

By now, St James’ Park had livened up, but the home team’s performance still lacked conviction in the final third.

Jaissle sent on Ramsey and Jacob Murphy for the last 15 minutes, but Newcastle found themselves pinned back by Everton, who were a threat on the break.

Half-chances came and went for Newcastle – who did not have a shot on target until the 86th minute, and also had Ramsey sent off for two stoppage-time yellow cards – as the travelling fans made themselves heard high up on Level 7.

The question some Newcastle fans are asking is just how high this team can finish above the Premier League’s relegation zone, as there are still big issues for Jaissle to address at both ends of the pitch ahead of what looks like being a challenging winter.

“The only way is togetherness, showing unity, and then the belief comes,” said Jaissle.

#825. Michael Mann Hospitalized After Accidentally Shooting Himself

Heat director Michael Mann was briefly hospitalized after a gun accidentally discharged from his holster while at a gun range Oct. 31.

The Collateral director experienced a real health scare on Halloween while shooting at a sanctioned gun range in Los Angeles.

“On Saturday, at a gun range, a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered resulting in a superficial injury to film director Michael Mann,” Mann’s representatives told E! News in a statement on Nov. 2. “He was treated and released Sunday.”

Following the Oct. 31 incident, Mann was taken to the hospital in “stable condition,” a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Police Department told the New York Times. The spokesperson also noted that responding units confirmed the shooting was accidental in nature, and Mann’s injury was minor.

E! News has reached out to the LAPD for comment but has not yet heard back.

Known for his highly stylized crime dramas like Heat and Thief, Mann has pursued target shooting as a hobby for decades. Previously, he shared insight into firearm practice to ensure his Robert DeNiro and Al Pacino-leading film was realistic, especially for the pivotal shootout scene.

“When I found the location in downtown LA, I blocked the choreography across two city blocks,” Mann told The Guardian last year of shooting for the 1995 film. “They’re leapfrogging: one guy’s laying down rounds while the other is moving forward and, then, he lays down rounds, et cetera, and it keeps going.”

As he recalled, “We trained at the LA county sheriff’s shooting ranges under appropriately rigid safety procedures and sheriff’s range masters.”

To ensure the scene became the memorable clip known today, Mann admitted that he and the actors practiced “three days a week” for “months.”

And the 83-year-old mused of the final product, “They could probably outshoot 95 percent of the [Los Angeles police department].”

Although it was Pacino and DeNiro were acting, Mann—who is revisiting the story in the forthcoming Heat 2—emphasized that the final product was as realistic as it could’ve possible been.

“For the actors, they were living it and were using full-load blanks during the filming, which reverberated off the glass walls of the urban canyons we were in,” he explained. “The initial sound of the rehearsals was so frightening that I threw maybe 10, 11 mics around the location and so we wound up using the sound recorded during the filming.”

For more stars who have experienced health scares, keep reading…

The Jessie alum opened up about her "hellish" migraines, sharing how they've worsened after suffering five concussions over the course of her life.

"The brain injuries make things significantly worse," Ryan shared during a September 2026 episode of Mythical Kitchen’s Last Meals. "I had a pretty crazy, life-altering brain injury a few years ago, and I was out of commission for six months."

While Ryan described her first four concussions as "incidents," she said her fifth one was trauma caused by "sustained shaking over a minute of time."

Now, the former Disney Channel star needs to close her eyes to "think better."

"Quite often the world is really loud. It’s really too bright. There’s a lot going on," she explained. "The visual data that I'm taking in can be so distracting and so loud. Then, with the migraines—which are significantly worsened by that—it sort of is too much."

Brianna "Chickenfry" LaPaglia's Ovarian Cyst

In May 2026, the BFFs podcaster underwent emergency surgery after doctors discovered a large ovarian cyst that had been twisting her organs and causing internal bleeding.

"There was a half a liter of blood in my pelvic floor," Brianna shared in a TikTok video after the operation. "I have five incisions all over my stomach. They went in through my belly button with a camera so they could find all the blood."

The Total Bellas alum revealed that one of her breast implants shifted after an elbow slam from fellow WWE star Piper Niven during a July 2025 wrestling match.

"It's OK," she told sister Bella Garcia at the time. "We're going to get it fixed one day. I told the doctor, I go, 'Newly divorced, so the minute the boots are hung up, I'm going to come back to you and we're going to make these girls look real good, because these girls are going to get some action in the future and that can't look like that.'"

In October 2026, the former The Bachelorette star detailed how she cracked a vertebra in her spine after setting her vibration plate—a motorized platform that rapidly moves back and forth to promote muscle activation and circulation—to "level 30, supersonic speed."

"Seemingly, subtly, somewhere on the way to 30, maybe 10 or 20, my vertebrae turn crooked and rub against each other," Windey shared in a Substack essaye aptly titled "Broke back, no mountain."

"It was too fast vibrations I guess, and too many vibrations maybe, and too much pressure to shake," she continued. "And it broke. Broke right off, like your ex-boyfriend’s bumper. Well, technically, it cracked."

The injury left her with what she described as "insatiable" paresthesia—a medical term for a tingling, pins-and-needles sensation.

"This is the greatest sense of condemnation; of persecution, I’ll ever feel," she added. "And I do wish it on my worst enemy If only they hadn’t wished it on me first."

The 12 Years a Slave star was diagnosed with uterine fibroids—non-cancerous growths that develop in or around the uterus—in 2014, the same year she won an Oscar for performance in the movie.

However, it wasn't until 2025 when she disclosed her diagnosis, writing on Instagram that she had been "suffering in silence" for more than a decade.

"When we reach puberty, we're taught periods mean pain, and that pain is simply part of being a woman," she shared. "We're struggling alone with something that affects us most."

The Beverly Hills, 90210 alum revealed in April 2025 that he was recovering from surgery after his appendix nearly burst.

“Last week, I started feeling some pain in my stomach,” Brian said in an Instagram video at the time. “I ended up going to the emergency room, and I had a perforated appendix. Not quite burst, but just before.”

He added, “I'm on the road to recovery. It's not an easy process. This is my first major surgery.”

In July 2025, the Daisy Jones & The Six star shared that she had been hospitalized due to a hernia—a gap in the muscular wall that's commonly found in the abdomen or groin area—caused by wearing tight pants.

"'Suki you never tweet anymore,'" she wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter. "Have you ever considered I wore pants so tight 6 months ago it caused a hernia & I’ve been too scared to tell you?"

Savannah DeMelo's Mid-Game "Medical Emergency" Mid-Game

The Racing Louisville midfielder collapsed just a few minutes into her soccer team's September 2025 match against Seattle Reign at Lumen Field in Seatle.

The United States Women’s National Team player could be seen slowly sitting down on the field with a teammate by her side, per Reuters, as the referee called for trainers to check her out. She collapsed seconds later.

“Savannah received immediate on-field care from medical personnel and was transported to a local hospital for further evaluation,” the National Women’s Soccer League wrote on X later that night. “She is stable and alert."

Adam Devine's Long-Term Injury From Childhood Accident

Adam Devine shared that injuries he sustained after getting hit by a cement truck when he was 11 years old are still affecting him to this day.

“It’s been a nightmare,” Devine said in a 2025 episode of the In Depth With Graham Bensinger podcast. “I have spasms all over. For a while, [the doctors] told me I was dying—literally, within this last year.”

He noted that pain comes and goes, adding, "My body has all these things that are a little wonky and a little wrong with it."

The Bachelor Nation alum shared that he went to the hospital “crawling on all fours” due to overwhelming back pain that was aggravated during an RV trip with a friend.

“Right now, knees to my toes, it’s, like, still tingly, which is crazy,” he said on a March 2025 episode of his Trading Secrets podcast. “And to put in perspective, I don’t know, man, like not to sound douchey, but like two, three weeks ago, maybe a month ago, I was squatting probably like 295 pounds. And right now, I can’t do a squat on my foot. I can’t do a one legged squat, I fall. It’s like I had a stroke or something.”

But with the help of a back specialist and some steroids, he added, “We’re on the mend.”

Real Housewives of Orange County’s Gina Kirschenheiter shared her ex-husband Matt Kirschenheiter suffered a heart attack in March 2025, but thankfully survived the ordeal.

The 30 Rock star suffered a health scare at a New York Knicks basketball game in March 2025, leading to him being wheeled out of Madison Square Garden.

However, the comedian shared an update on social media the following day, noting it was a case of food poisoning and that he was on the mend.

The Even Stevens alum shared in February 2025 that she was shot in the face while on a trip to shoot clay pigeons to celebrate husband Brendan Rooney's birthday.

"There was another party with us and they unsafely fired in the wrong direction and shot me in the face," she wrote on Instagram. "@thebrendanrooney immediately sprung into action, assessed me, and rushed me to the hospital. I was hit in 5 places, one was less than an inch from hitting me directly in my right eye."

The Kim Possible alum continued, "Unfortunately a fragment got lodged behind my eye and it is too risky to remove surgically at this time. Doctors will continue to monitor me (I can see normally at the moment)."

The actress said she was grateful to be alive. "I love my daughters, husband, family, and friends so much," she said. "I saw my life flash before my eyes and I’m telling you, hug the people around you every chance you can. Life can change in an instant."

While the internet isn't always a kind place, Amy Schumer is happy that, in this case, it helped her get answers."The internet really came for me after doing a bunch of press, and I was like, 'OK everybody, relax,'" Amy recalled of her "puffier" face on a January 2025 episode of Call Her Daddy. "But then doctors were chiming in in the comments and they were like, 'No no, we think something’s really up. Your face looks so crazy that we think something’s up. And I’m like, ‘Wait, I’m getting trolled by doctors?’"After these doctors said they thought she had Cushing syndrome and that it may be caused by spiking coritsol levels or steroid injections, the Life & Beth creator thought, "Wait, I have been getting steroid injections in my scars.""I had a breast reduction, a C-section, whatever, and so I was getting these steroid injections," Amy said. "So it gave me this thing called Cushing syndrome, which I wouldn’t have known if the internet hadn’t come for me so hard."Toda, Amy is just relieved she's OK. As she shared in a February 2024 News Not Noise newsletter, "Finding out I have the kind of Cushing that will just work itself out and I'm healthy was the greatest news imaginable."

Casey Fitzgerald's Neck Injury From Hockey Skate Blade

The AHL player was cut by a fellow player's skate during a game in December 2024 and received 25 stitches. His father, New Jersey Devils general manager Tom Fitzgerald later told ESPN after his son was fully recovered, "We're very lucky. I don't wish that on any parent."

Hailey Bieber had the "scariest moment" of her life when she was having breakfast with husband Justin Bieber and started experiencing stroke-like symptoms in March 2022."Justin was like, 'Are you OK?'" the Rhode skincare mogul shared a month later on YouTube, "and I just didn't respond because I wasn't sure. And then he asked me again and when I went to respond, I couldn't speak. The right side of my face started drooping. I couldn't get a sentence out."While Hailey said the facial drooping stopped and her speech came back, she went to the hospital to make sure she was OK."They did some scans and they were able to see that I had suffered a small blood clot to my brain," the model added, "which they labeled and categorized as something called a TIA [Transient Ischemic Attack]."Later, Hailey went to the University of California, Los Angeles, where she found out she had a hole in her heart called a patent foramen ovale (PFO).She explained the blood clot had traveled into her heart, "escaped" through the hole and went to her brain, leading to the TIA.Hailey said she had a successful PFO closure procedure and was now feeling great.

The same year Hailey had her health scare, Justin experienced one of his own.In June 2022, the "Baby" singer shared he was diagnosed with Ramsay Hunt syndrome, a condition that caused temporary paralysis to parts of his face and forced him to cancel the remainder of his Justice World Tour."It is from this virus that attacks the nerve in my ear and my facial nerves and has caused my face to have paralysis," Justin explained in an Instagram video at the time. "As you can see, this eye is not blinking. I can't smile on this side of my face. This nostril will not move. So, there's full paralysis on this side of my face."In fact, he told his followers it had gotten "progressively harder to eat." But after a while, the paralysis went away."He's doing really well," Hailey said on a June 2022 episode of Good Morning America, later adding, "He's feeling a lot better. Obviously, it was just a very scary and random situation to happen, but he's going to be totally OK and I'm just grateful that he's fine."

While Jamie Foxx initially kept details of his April 2023 hospitalization private, he later opened up about what he went through.One day in Atlanta, "I was having such a bad headache, so I asked my boy, I said, ‘Listen, I need an aspirin,’” the Oscar winner said in his 2024 Netflix special What Had Happened Was... “Before I could get the Aspirin, I went out. I don’t remember 20 days.”Jamie said he was initially taken to a doctor who gave him a cortisone shot and then sent him home. However, his concerned sister Deidra Dixon then drove him to a hospital, where they got an answer: He had a brain bleed that led to a stroke.Twenty days after undergoing an operation, the Django Unchained woke up May 4 in a wheelchair and couldn’t walk. He then went to Chicago for rehabilitation and therapy."All I can tell you is that I appreciate every prayer,” he said, “because I needed every prayer.”

Tracey Yukich's Medical Emergency on The Biggest Loser

The reality star revealed that she "died" while running a mile during the first challenge of the NBC competition series.

“I don't remember a lot,” she explained on Fit for TV: The Reality of The Biggest Loser. “I remember hearing the helicopter. I just felt like I was floating. And then my grandpa was there. And then I saw darkness. But then I saw light. So I knew, I knew I died that day.”

“My organs were literally shutting down,” she continued. “I didn't realize that I had rhabdomyolysis. And rhabdomyolysis is your body's way of saying, ‘I'm going to shut down on you.’”

Emilia Clarke filmed battle scenes for Game of Thrones, but in 2019, she published an essay in The New Yorker titled "A Battle for My Life."Having a bad headache at the gym, "I reached the toilet, sank to my knees, and proceeded to be violently, voluminously ill," the actress wrote. "Meanwhile, the pain—shooting, stabbing, constricting pain—was getting worse. At some level, I knew what was happening: my brain was damaged."She was taken to the hospital for a brain scan."The diagnosis was quick and ominous: a subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), a life-threatening type of stroke, caused by bleeding into the space surrounding the brain," the Emmy nominee added. "I’d had an aneurysm, an arterial rupture."Emilia had immediate surgery to seal the aneurysm, calling the pain "unbearable." While she was recovering, she continued, she experienced aphasia and was "muttering nonsense."A week later, "the aphasia passed," Emilia added, and she left the hospital a month after being admitted. At a 2013 brain scan, she learned a growth "doubled in size" and that she needed surgery again."When they woke me, I was screaming in pain," she wrote. "The procedure had failed. I had a massive bleed and the doctors made it plain that my chances of surviving were precarious if they didn’t operate again. This time they needed to access my brain in the old-fashioned way—through my skull."Thankfully, Emilia shared, she's now "at a hundred per cent."

Snoop Dogg's daughter Cori Broadus is grateful for her family.Because after she suffered a "severe stroke" in January 2024, her loved ones rushed to be by her side."I texted them that I just had a stroke and sent them a picture," she told E! News correspondent Will Marfuggi in December 2024. "Everybody just came to my rescue."Because of other medical concerns, Cori ended up staying in the hospital longer than she initially expected."I could have went home after my stroke, but my lupus wasn't doing so well," the Snoop's Fatherhood: Cori and Wayne's Story star continued. "My kidneys were failing. It was a lot going on."Today, Cori is on the mend."I'm doing great," she added. "I just had a little bit of motor skills that I had to work back on. But other than that, I was fine."

Shailene Woodley’s early 20s were not an easy time health-wise.“It got to the point where I was losing my hearing. I couldn’t walk for longer than five minutes at a time without having to lay down for hours, and hours and sleep. Everything I ate hurt my stomach,” the actress said on a September 2024 episode of the SHE MD Podcast. “It was this conflation of issues and diagnoses and different doctors telling me different things.”So Shailene—who chose to keep the exact condition private—set out to find answers. “I come from a very holistic background and study herbalism,” she added. “So I was very keen on, ‘I’m going to work with real MDs, [and] I’m also going to work with independent kind of healers.’ Just trying to search for some sense of comfort in my own skin.”It was a long journey—one that lasted for 10 years.“Throughout that decade, a lot of other things came from feeling so much discomfort physically,” the Big Little Lies star noted, “which was, ‘My gosh, if everything I eat hurts my stomach, I’m now suddenly afraid of food.’ And then going into the kind of mental f--ckery that can happen with that of body dysmorphia and confusion about identity and feeling safe in my own capsule, in my own skin, what that meant, and what that should be.”After tending to both her physical and mental health, Shailene is feeling much better.“It was a journey that ultimately physically resolved itself, and I am very healthy,” she shared. “I’m so happy to be able to say that."

#824. Serbia: Tens of thousands rally ahead of elections

After two years of student-led protests, Serbia will soon vote in what observers describe as a referendum-like snap election pitting strongman Aleksandar Vucic against the student movement.

Over a hundred thousand of Serbians took to the streets in support of Serbia's protesting youth movement on Thursday, in what was the final campaign rally ahead of a pivotal election challenge to the Balkan nation's populist strongman, Aleksandar Vucic.

Crowds poured into Belgrade's central square from all directions and filled up several blocks around the area. Independent crowd-monitoring group Archive of Public Gatherings estimated about 150,000 people were at the rally.

The optimistic crowds chanted "victory" ahead of Sunday's crunch vote which comes after two years of student-led protests against Vucic. It was triggered by a 2024 collapse of a canopy at the newly renovated Novi Sad railway station which killed 16 people.

The anti-corruption movement, led by university students, has since snowballed from demands for an independent investigation into the incident, into calls for early elections.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The Student List, a leaderless movement of student-backed candidates, is the veteran leader's biggest threat.

Thousands supporting it flocked to Belgrade's streets on Thursday.

"I came to support the Student List because young people finally gave me hope that it is possible to live in a normal country," 47-year-old Marija Nedeljkovic Radic told the French AFP news agency as she arrived for the students' rally.

"Really, for the first time in my life, I believe that it is possible," she said.

"We are putting an end to 14 years of humiliation, chaos and betrayal, and to decades of putting personal and party interests above yours," university professor Jugoslav Gasic, one of 250 candidates on the Student List, told the crowd who chanted "Victory, victory!"

"You deserve better, and we know how to deliver it. Students are winning!"

Vucic has dominated Serbian politics for over a decade now, either as prime minister or president of the Balkan country.

As pressure from the protests mounted, he announced a snap election last month. He has resigned as president, but many argue it is a tactical move so that he could run for prime minister.

This is now the biggest electoral challenge his party, the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), has faced since it was elected into power in 2012.

The leader, meanwhile, has regularly accused the students movement of being a foreign-funded coup.

"Let us never forget how they tried to bring down our state. Let us always protect and defend it," Vucic said to a sports hall full of supporters on Thursday. "Let us go out and defeat them! Defeat them decisively!"

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Days before the vote, Serbian civil societies warned that conditions for "free and fair election" were lacking.

"This assessment is not based on isolated incidents, opposition claims or political disagreement with the government," a joint statement by 24 organisations said, arguing it was supported by documented findings.

Analysts warn that a close election result could lead to post-election instability, if both sides declare victory. Vucic, who controls the Serbian police, has said he would quash any unrest after the vote.

While several minor parties are also in the race for premiership, observers say that there is a referendum-like atmosphere between Vucic and the students' movement which could sideline other parties in the 250-member parliament.

Tallulah Willis is calling out the haters.

#822. Lenny Kravitz's Rep Denies Rumor He Was Victim of Florida Plane Crash

After Lenny Kravitz was rumored to be on board a private plane that crashed in Florida on Nov. 1, killing all nine passengers, his rep set the record straight on the “incorrect” report.

Lenny Kravitz has both feet safely on the ground.

After a private plane traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed into a Florida neighborhood mid-flight on Nov. 1—killing all nine people on board­—reports began to circulate that the beloved singer had been one of the passengers.

Kravitz’s rep Carleen Donovan, however, told BocaNewsNow that such reports are “untrue and incorrect.”

The confusion arose after a female pilot, who was misidentified as the pilot of the downed plane, had shared a since-deleted message to social media sharing she was to fly Kravitz from Austin to the Bahamas, per Page Six. But while the route and date were similar, their plane journey was not the one which ended in such tragedy.

Instead, one of the co-pilots of the crashed Learjet 60 plane has been identified by her father as Nathalia Filgueiras. The identities of the other eight passengers aboard have yet to be shared.

The crash resulted, as seen in footage of the accident, in a crater in the middle of a road near Cresthaven, Florida. The site was engulfed in flames in some photos of the accident.

Following the crash, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy confirmed on social media that the crash occurred at 12:50 p.m. ET local time and that all nine people on board had died. He also confirmed the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) would be sending a team to support the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigation.

“Today's plane crash in Palm Beach County, Florida is a horrific tragedy,” Duffy added in his message. “Please join me in praying for the families and loved ones of those we lost.”

According to NBC News, citing air traffic control audio, a female pilot onboard the plan reported “light, clear ice” was accumulating on the aircraft but noted it was “manageable.” Within minutes, however, the pilot began shouting “mayday” and reported the plane was descending 10,000-20,000 feet per minute.

In the wake of the tragedy, Florida Governor Ron DeSantis called the crash “cataclysmic.” He also confirmed there had been no reported injuries or deaths among people on the ground.

“It looked like a missile going down,” DeSantis told reporters. “It left a big crater on the side of the road.”

The plane went down within 500 feet of Anthony Blackmon’s residence, who then recounted the ordeal. “Debris was everywhere. Debris hit my house,” he told NBC South Florida. “Everything was on fire. The road was on fire.”

Meanwhile, Learjet manufacturer Bombardier said it was “deeply saddened by this tragic event and extend our sincerest sympathies to all those affected.”

“We cannot comment on the potential cause of this accident until the investigation is complete,” the statement continued, per NBC News, “and we will fully support the investigating authorities and cooperate as needed.”

The low-profile shape traces back to the plimsoll, one of the earliest sneaker styles in the fashion cycle. Some fit close to the foot like a glove, while others take inspiration from “sneakerinas,” the ballet-flat-meets-sneaker trend.

Designer brands have helped push the silhouette back into the spotlight. Labels like Miu Miu and Louis Vuitton have helped popularize ballet-inspired sneaker hybrids, the ladder introduced its own LV Sneakerina in 2025, cementing the style into a high-profile luxury trend.

Arsenal move clear at the top with a rare win at Liverpool

Kai Havertz's first-half goal made the difference as Arsenal won at Anfield in the Premier League for the first time since 2012.

Here's how we rated the Liverpool and Arsenal players, and your scores are below.

Premier League: Arsenal go top with rare win at Liverpool

Were Arsenal lucky not to give away a penalty?

#819. Somewhere over the transcontinental burrito tunnel

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Elitsa Dermendzhiyska is a BSFA-nominated writer, a former science writer in psychology, and the co-creator of a mental-health fantasy game. Her stories have appeared in Flash Fiction Online, Small Wonders, Flame Tree Press and others.

Lenny fell in love with Bea around burrito number five. He recognized that dizzying jolt to his brain the instant the tunnel’s mouth sighed with a sweet pneumatic hiss and the vacuum-sealed burrito glided in.

Three hours and twenty-one minutes earlier, 2,553 miles away, at her end of the tunnel in the East Bay facility, Bea had been thinking of him. She must have. He wished he could trace her regard for his existence beyond the minute or two it would’ve taken her to pluck the flash-chilled burrito from the sorting dock, nest it in its carbon-fibre pod, and send it in the near-vacuum of the tunnel deep into the Earth to be blasted across the continent at just below the speed of sound.

Lenny worked the subterranean off-ramp in New Jersey, where multitudes of the famed Mission burritos of the Bay Area arrived levitating on magnetic currents, ready for dispatch to the ravenous gullets of the five boroughs of New York City. Since the blast aboveground, the flow had dwindled to one burrito at a time. Lenny stared at each with longing, wondering if Bea had tucked a note for him into the Mylar pocket.

When her first message arrived, the eerie rumble still vibrated through the basement walls. Lenny was pacing in circles, running through scenarios — alien invasion, given the contact the year before; nuclear war, given … many things — and going mad at the thought of dying underground, alone. He was ready to venture out and face the radiation or the new overlords when the first burrito slid out with a note attached to it. Here: an end-of-the-world burrito. Best you’ve ever had.

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Read more science fiction from Nature Futures

Apparently Bea had never expected her message to reach anyone. Who knew insomnia would drive them both to work before clock-in time, saving them? Now she was sitting on a dragon’s hoard of burritos, that morning’s shipment enough to feed them both for weeks. They could stay put, wait for things to blow over.

The problem wasn’t food — or the aliens, or the bombs. It was, as usual with Lenny, love.

Around burrito number nine, he wrote on a whim, Folks might get the wrong impression if they saw you spoiling me. He slipped his note into a Mylar pouch, which he placed inside an empty burrito pod and sent down the tube.

Bea volleyed back, Yeah, they’ll think you’re my grandson. PS What folks, Lenny???

He chewed through the cold tortilla. Was she flirting back? Or letting him down gently by hinting at her age? Which wouldn’t be an issue.

Lenny agonized over his retort for hours, maybe even days. Afterwards, every exchange between him and Bea felt loaded with subtext. Chorizo with Mexican red rice, refried pinto beans and real Monterey Jack, Bea wrote. Enjoy :) Was a smiley face coy or merely friendly? What about one with a wink?

Lenny talked to her in his head, Bea nodding, her dark eyes dancing. But whenever he put pen to paper, his lucidity evaporated, crumbling to the overeager babble of a hapless nitwit.

At one point, Bea wrote, A day is a long time.

He stared at the plastic sleeve, yearning to sweep her into his arms. He placed his hands where her own had been three hours and twenty-one minutes earlier.

Are you bored, too? Lenny replied. I thought we could pass the time by getting to know each other. He proceeded to tell her about his favourite music and where he’d grown up, including several major formative events from his childhood.

After what felt like eternity, Bea wrote back. It was an ingredient list. Carne asada, sautéed mushrooms and salsa verde.

What’s happening, Bea? What’d I do? he wrote.

Several torturous hours passed. Then: Imagine a map of an island, alright? It’s the most high-fidelity, super-detailed map of the place there is. Now imagine the map itself is on the island. You see what that means? There must be a map of the map inside the map. And inside that second map — another one. On and on. It’s maps all the way down, Lenny.

Lenny had heard a paradox like this somewhere before. But Bea seemed to be opening up at last. Her scrawls looked frantic, streaking across the margins like startled flamingos. He turned the riddle around and around, then wrote back, What about the map maker? Is he also in all of the maps drawing them … and himself?

#818. Stevie Nicks Details Writing “Landslide” About Lindsey Buckingham

Stevie Nicks shared rare insight into writing “Landslide” during her and fellow Fleetwood Mac member Lindsey Buckingham’s romance: “It was a long time ago.”

Stevie Nicks is reflecting on the seasons of her life.

And one of her most pivotal was writing “Landslide” in 1975 amid her tumultuous romance with fellow Fleetwood Mac member Lindsey Buckingham.

“I wrote this song in Aspen, Colorado, when I was deciding whether or not Lindsey and I should continue,” Nicks said at the City of Hope 2026 Music, Film and Entertainment Industry (MFEI) Spirit of Life Gala Oct. 27, per People. “Well, it was a long time ago and 930,000 years later, we still continued.”

Though the pair's romance—which began in the early 1970s before the pair joined Fleetwood Mac—eventually ended, the power of Nicks and Buckingham's creative partnership is what helped cement the group’s enduring legacy.

As for how the tune came to her, Nicks explained that she wrote the song “looking out over the snow-covered hills in this beautiful house” up in the mountains. Her friends had gone out to dinner and, left to her own devices before such a mirror in the sky, inspiration struck.

“I’m like, ‘Okay, because I’m so poor that just sitting in this house when you’re looking out at this view is so fantastic, I’m going to write a fantastic song,” Nicks said. “I just happened to bring my Goya [guitar], which I could hardly play, but I thought it looked good so I wrote this song.”

Nicks, 78, and Buckingham, 77, first met as high school students in California before their romance began in 1972. They released their first album Buckingham Nicks as a folk-rock duo in 1973, the same year they signed a record deal with Polydor Records.

Despite being dropped from their label when the album didn’t generate much commercial success, they eventually met Mick Fleetwood in 1974 and later joined Fleetwood Mac, which also consisted of Christine McVie and John McVie. The rest, as they say, is history.

And even after Nicks and Buckingham parted ways romantically in 1976, they channeled their pain into the band’s 1977 album Rumours, which famously included breakup tracks like "Go Your Own Way" and "Silver Springs.”

As for where they stand today? Well, they might have been 'fraid of changing in the past, but they’ve since sailed through the ocean tides to calmer waters.

As Buckingham recently shared, he and Nicks “are talking all the time now.”

“Fleetwood Mac has been working on a documentary,” he told E! News in August, referring to Apple TV’s upcoming 2027 project “I think the process of making that has been a very circular healing process for all of us.”

And while it took gettin’ older for Nicks and Buckingham to make peace, they’re now one of many former Hollywood couples who have reached friendly territory. Read on for more.

No, they are never, ever, ever getting back together. But at this point—between the birthday parties, the friendly embraces and even freaking acting out a sexual fantasy in a star-studded virtual reading of Fast Times at Ridgemont High—it feels like the former Hollywood golden couple is just taunting us.

You know you're cool when you can pop into your ex's talk show and give him a hard time. Such was the case when Silverman turned up on Kimmel's stage in 2018 to chat about her show I Love You, America and his "cute," "bright," "funny" wife Molly McNearney. "It's not fair!" the actress cracked. "She gets, like, new woke Jimmy. I had Man Show Jimmy."

She even sent over a gift after the newlyweds welcomed daughter Lyla in August 2020. Thrilled for son Jack to become a big brother, a source told E! News at the time that Faris "is very supportive."

It would have been super easy for the exes' relationship to become a flop. But more than four years after a messy split, the HGTV stars are still killing it at two projects: parenting kids Taylor and Brayden and turning run-down properties into someone else's dream home.

Literally "best friends" as the rocker put it in a 2013 interview with Oprah Winfrey, the parents to actress Zoe Kravitz still consider themselves kin. "We're one big happy family," Lenny said of his ex, who went on to wed Jason Momoa before their 2020 split. "It's beautiful, and it just shows you what can be done."

After the Dancing With the Stars co-host and former hockey player called in quits in 2020, the pair have continually proved they are on good terms.

In 2025, Hough enjoyed a trip to the lake with Laich and his then-pregnant fiancée Katrín Tanja Davíðsdóttir.

And when Laich announced his marriage to the former Crossfit athlete in 2025, Hough celebrated the news, writing on Instagram, “Congratulations! So so happy for you both. Sending you all the love, health and happiness for the years to come to you and your beautiful family."

Since their 2015 breakup, the parents to Violet, Seraphina and Samuel have hit the conscious uncoupling trifecta: Joint vacations, shared holidays and public displays of admiration with Ben dubbing his ex "an amazing mother" during a 2016 interview with E! News.

"I can’t remember why I was Bavarian, but I do know today is your birthday," Garner wrote on Instagram in 2023 along a still from Alias, in which she was dressed in a dirndl. "I hope it’s a great one, Michael! XX."

The Vampire Diaries costars may have called it quits in 2013 after three years of dating, but they've remained close friends since then. In 2014, somerhalder started dating Nikki Reed and tied the knot later that year. Naturally, Dobrev befriended the Twilight actress.

The Grammy winner and songwriter ex—who finalized their divorce in January 2024—have remained on good terms as they continue to parent their son Hayes. In fact, the pair live just five minutes apart from one another, which makes co-parenting a breeze.

#817. Defeat for London City - but is Europe a real possibility?

Clinical Man City edge past London City in WSL thriller

It shows how quickly London City Lionesses have progressed that they were hugely disappointed with a narrow defeat by defending champions Manchester City.

For a team that were playing second-tier football 18 months ago, their lofty ambitions of qualifying for the Champions League suddenly don't seem far-fetched.

London City looked like the better team for most of the afternoon at Hayes Lane but were given a harsh lesson by the visitors in how to be ruthless.

Manchester City needed goals from Khadija Shaw and Lauren Hemp against the run of play, but they dug in to win 2-1 and to continue setting the pace at the top of the Women's Super League.

Those goals came after countless opportunities went begging for London City, who ended the game having had 24 shots but only six on target.

The performance was enough, however, to show that London City are more than capable of competing with the WSL's elite.

The next question is whether they can do it consistently.

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

London City Lionesses are a club who do things differently and, backed by US billionaire Michele Kang, they are not shy to disrupt the current order.

They are an independent women's football club who have spent big in the transfer window and agreed a record-breaking shirt deal with Nike believed to be worth more than Â£3m a year.

They have built their own training facility in Kent and persuaded superstars such as Alexia Putellas to join in the summer.

Spain international Putellas showcased her latest Ballon d'Or trophy - the third of her career - before kick-off on Sunday.

London City Lionesses are clearly no minnows, but even a squad full of superstars needs time to gel.

It was for this reason that people doubted whether they were ready this season to qualify for the Champions League and break the WSL's traditional top three.

But on Sunday's showing, they are not as far off as people thought.

Manager Eder Maestre said the team's performances are already at the level they want but results have not always shown that and they still have work to do.

"That's why it's a very frustrating situation. We were speaking a lot about respecting the identity and it doesn't matter the team that we were facing," the Spaniard said.

"The next step in that project was showing everybody that we can perform, while respecting that identity that we are trying to build on.

"That's why it's doubly frustrating, because I think the result was not the one we deserve. Manchester City are more mature.

"They are more used to it. When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, maybe you have more experience.

"That's why we have extra nervousness in the moments that we need to be more clinical."

Where London City fell was where Manchester City stood tall.

Moments of brilliance by world-class players Shaw and Hemp delivered the goods and when London City's pressure grew, so too did Manchester City's resilience.

It is that consistency across 90 minutes, and the season as a whole, that Manchester City manager Andree Jeglertz believes will demonstrate the difference.

"They are a very good team and they really showed the highest level," said Jeglertz.

"What it means to be at the top of this league, is playing week after week, and at the same level - and finding different levels to win.

"That is what we have created. That's what everybody who wants to win something needs to be able to do. To contest, you need to compete for the whole season."

London City Lionesses dominated the first half as shown by the momentum swings

London City Lionesses are providing plenty of optimism on the pitch, but even if they were to qualify for the Champions League this season, are they allowed to?

Current Uefa rules state that owners cannot have two clubs competing in the same competition, meaning one of Kang's Lyon or London City Lionesses would potentially miss out.

It is a dilemma that many have discussed, but if they continue to perform so well, it could prove to be a problem earlier than expected.

"First of all, what we feel is important, is to be part of the conversation," London City's chief executive officer Martin Semmens told BBC Sport.

"The next stage is getting towards trophies. Our ambition is to be in Europe, to play in Europe every year, and to compete with the likes of Barcelona and Arsenal.

"We're probably one step behind that in squad development and all the other things we have to do. But on our day, we feel we can beat them."

London City's ambitions are clear - so what happens if they do qualify this season?

"I think Michele [Kang] has a really clear view and that is that she wants to see as much investment come into the women's game as possible," added Semmens.

"The men's multi-club ownership rules is about being careful not to have control over two clubs. We see it differently on the women's side.

"We want to see more investment, so we believe if you invest in more than one club, the game will accelerate faster.

"We truly understand and respect the rules, always. But there are logical, structured ways that we can compete in Europe next season."

#816. Suki Waterhouse Reveals What She Learned From Bradley Cooper Romance

Suki Waterhouse, who has been with Robert Pattinson since 2018, recently revealed the lesson from on her two-year romance with Bradley Cooper and how it’s shaped her experience in the public eye.

Suki Waterhouse learned a bit about how to love, to love, to love in the public eye from Bradley Cooper.

The Daisy Jones & The Six star shared a rare look back at her first experience with a high-profile romance in her early 20s—she dated Cooper, who was in his late 30s, from 2013 to 2015—admitting she was going into loveland without a road map.

“When you’re younger, you go into everything so blindly and you don’t think of the consequences, including maybe of relationships,” Waterhouse explained in an interview with The Times published Oct. 31, not naming Cooper explicitly. “You don’t really have any concept of any repercussions of being in things that are public.”

In the more than a decade since, Waterhouse has built a life with Robert Pattinson—with whom she welcomed a daughter in 2024—and learned, “You can have a private life and a public life at the same time.”

And though she didn’t during her romance with Cooper, the 34-year-old shared, “I know how to separate those two.”

Once she met the Twilight alum in 2018, Waterhouse assured she was more than ready to go the distance.

“I can’t believe that I have this in my life and I can’t believe that I’m so happy,” she emphasized. “And maybe I was surprised because before I had only ever gone out with someone for two years and if it was two years it would have been a disaster at the end.”

Although Waterhouse is crediting her ability to keep her personal life private to her relationship with the 51-year-old, the “OMG” singer has always kept romance close to her chest.

“I don't talk about my boyfriend because it's boring,” she told Elle U.K. in 2014. "At least, that's what I decided to tell you when you asked. I do think whatever I say will sound weird. But the truth is, if I start talking about him, I probably won't be able to stop. And I don't really want to talk about him, you know?”

Waterhouse and Cooper dated from 2013 to 2015 and even made a red carpet debut at the Oscars in 2015 just weeks before their split was confirmed.

At the time, a source told E! News that Cooper——who went on to date Irina Shayk, with whom he shares 9-year-old daughter Lea, shortly after their split before beginning his romance with Gigi Hadid in 2023—wanted to start a family but Waterhouse was not on the same page.

#815. Boy, 14, hands himself in to police over Bradley Lowery video

A huge Sunderland fan, Bradley Lowery was honoured by the club in May

A 14-year-old boy has "handed himself in" to West Midlands Police after a video posted on social media appeared to show a fan taunting Sunderland with a photo of Bradley Lowery during Saturday's Premier League match.

Sunderland fan Bradley died aged six in 2017 from neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer.

Coventry said on Sunday they were investigating the video footage while Bradley's mother, Gemma, released her own statement through the Bradley Lowery Foundation, which raises funds and awareness to help and support children with cancer.

West Midlands Police has confirmed an investigation is now under way.

"We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City's Premier League match with Sunderland," a police statement said.

"A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course.

"We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim's family, and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs."

Coventry said they were aware of the video and the club "does not tolerate offensive behaviour" and will co-operate with the relative authorities.

Gemma Lowery said her "beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate" in her statement.

"As Bradley's mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it's one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile," she said.

"I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between.

"So much of Bradley's short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face.

"To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

"We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I'm all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter?

"I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad's family help him understand how hurtful his actions were."

Lowery added she did not want any "hatred directed" towards the fan, but hoped the "club takes appropriate action".

#814. Germany sit out FIFA Under-15 World Cup as Russia return

Germany is one a handful of FIFA's 211 nations to refuse an invitation to play at the inaugural Under-15 World Cup. The tournament will also mark Russia's return to the FIFA fold.

With nearly 1,000 matches and 189 teams, the Under-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan is bloated even by FIFA's usual standards. It marks a change in its attitude to children's international tournaments, which have not existed on anywhere near this scale before.

For Germany, it is too much too soon. The German FA (DFB) told DW that it had "consciously decided not to participate." The statement from the organization suggested the DFB — whose development of young players is under scrutiny after a run of poor performances by the men's national team — felt such a tournament was not appropriate for players so young.

"At this age level, our identification and development process is still underway, and we therefore do not believe it is appropriate to nominate a fixed squad for an international tournament at this stage," it read.

"More broadly, the DFB's approach to talent development is based on the principle of supporting young players in a long-term and age-appropriate manner. We carefully assess at which stage international competitions and development measures are beneficial for each age group.

"In our view, young talents should not be exposed too early to the accompanying aspects of professional football. These include increased expectations and pressure, public evaluation of their performances, and early interest from agents and the football market."

The refusal to play in the tournament, which began this week, is consistent with Germany's more cautious approach to youth development. While in some leagues, like the Premier League in England, there is no regulation about youths playing professionally, in Germany's top flight, the Bundesliga, players must be 16. In fact, before the 2020-21 season, players could not be granted a pro license before they were 17 years and six months old.

That change enabled Youssoufa Moukoko to make his Bundesliga debut for Borussia Dortmund a day after his 16th birthday in 2020, becoming the league's youngest player in the process.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

But, some would argue his is a cautionary tale. Hyped wildly due to his goalscoring exploits at youth level, Moukoko was fast-tracked by Dortmund and Germany, who called him up for the 2022 World Cup. Now, still just 21, he is struggling for game time and goals on loan at Corum, in the Turkish Super League, from Danish side Copenhagen.

Players under 16 are also forbidden by FIFA from having an agent. But this is poorly regulated in some regions of the world. That led Bundesliga club St. Pauli, then in the second division, to announce they would no longer work with player agents or private agencies in their youth system in 2023.

"We want to focus on partnership and dialogue with the players, their families and their relatives," explained the head of the club's youth academy, Benjamin Liedtke, as St. Pauli officially positioned themselves "against the commercialization of youth football."

Germany are one of 22 nations to refuse the invitation to compete in the tournament, 18 of whom are from UEFA, Europe's confederation. The USA are also one of the prominent refusals alongside Ukraine, whose FA told German public broadcaster Sportschau that they initially refused on sporting grounds before claiming that "other countries indicated that they would compete but did not want to play against Russia." DW contacted a number of FAs to clarify this point but is yet to receive a response.

FIFA President Gianni Infantino, who has become a notorious figure thanks to a number of scandals over the past year, told Sky in February: "We have to [look at reinstating Russia], definitely, because this ban has not achieved anything. It has just created frustration and hatred. Having girls and boys from Russia being able to play football games in other parts of Europe would help."

Eight months later, he has his wish. The ongoing tournament, billed as the "FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival" comprises eight-a-side games with 20 minute halves, a smaller pitch and a number of other technical tweaks. FIFA say the 2027 edition will be for girls teams only.

"Young players need meaningful matches, different opponents and different football experiences in order to develop. Talent exists everywhere, but the opportunities available to young players are not always the same," said FIFA Chief of Global Football Development, Arsene Wenger, likely referencing that teams from Bhutan and Seychelles to the Bahamas and Vanuatu are present.

"This tournament gives players from across the world the chance to compete, to learn and to grow."

FIFA are yet to respond to a DW request for further comment.

The round robin stage, according to FIFA, has placed teams in "groups that provide diverse sporting and regional representation" but also appears to have, at least initially, kept apart nations in conflict with each other.

For example, Israel and Palestine or Kosovo and Serbia are not in the same groups but could, in theory, meet in the later stages of the tournament. This would not be allowed in senior football, thanks to various bans and workarounds.

FIFA are vague about how the tournament works after the round robin, saying only that it will consist of "four to five additional matches per team, determined by results and subsequent tier placement. [There will be] one winner for each of the six tiers." It also said that the winner of the top tier will be crowned champions but all teams will play matches until the tournament concludes on October 30.

But, given that they have been banned from international football since invading Ukraine in 2022, it is the presence of a Russian national team at a FIFA tournament that will likely heap the most controversy on to young shoulders. Though a Russian presence was not the reason for German refusal, not attending for sporting reasons may also turn out to be a smart piece of sport politics.

Unlike a love fern, Kate Hudson doesn’t think she has to let her amicable bond with exes Chris Robinson and Matt Bellamy die.“Chris and I just need to check in once in a while,” the How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days actress told The Sunday Times in 2022 of her former spouse and dad to son Ryder.As for Matt, dad to her son Bingham, he's "so wonderful—I couldn’t have asked for a better co-parent," she continued. "For me it’s like, you loved this person. That doesn’t just go away, but you can re-establish a different kind of love. You can have an amazing time with an ex-partner because you’re really only focused on the love of your child.”Kate is also mom to daughter Rani, whom she shares with fiancé Danny Fujikawa.“It might not look traditional from the outside, but on the inside I feel like we’re killing it,” she added. “The unit that I’ve created with three children with three different fathers is a seriously strong unit, and it’s ours.”

Sometimes, it can seem like co-parents are galaxies apart. But Anna Faris has suggested that her relationship with ex Chris Pratt, with whom she shares son Jack, and his wife Katherine Schwarzenegger has grown."We're all getting much closer, and I so appreciate that," The House Bunny  actress, who split from the Guardians of the Galaxy actor in 2017 and finalized their divorce the following year, told People in 2022. "They're very protective of me, and I want to be very protective of them. I so appreciate their support."In fact, Anna called Katherine—who also shares daughters Lyla and Eloise and son Ford with Chris—"awesome.""She's just on top of it," the Mom star continued about The Gift of Forgiveness author. "I love how she is with Jack."And ultimately, Anna—who is now married to cinematographer Michael Barrett—indicated she's happy with how things are going for the blended family."It feels just much easier now that time has passed," she told the outlet. "It feels really good to not live with that internal churning of unpleasantness."

It's good when co-parents wannabe on the same page, and Mel B admits it took a while for her and ex Eddie Murphy to form this kind of relationship.

"I think being in the kind of [situation] that I was in, it was hard for me to step out and have that relationship [with Eddie] flourish," the Spice Girls member told Us Weekly in May 2025 , while reflecting on her past struggles with PTSD and coercive control. "I managed to do it bit by bit."However, Mel B, who shares teenage Angel with Eddie, says their friendship has "flourished even more" in recent years."Angel is coming over [to Murphy’s house]," she continued. "They spend time together. They go on holiday together. He has [10] kids and he’s a proper father."

While The O.C. had plenty of drama, that doesn't mean that Rachel Bilson's co-parenting relationship with ex Hayden Christensen has to be the same way."Everything's good," the actress, who shares daughter Briar Rose with the Star Wars alum, told People in 2024. "Everything's in a really good place. She is so beautifully flourishing and has the support completely surrounding her from every side."

#812. Why Scottish football is struggling to produce young talent

Calum Ferguson was an Inverness Caley Thistle academy player but only played twice for the first team

Calum Ferguson achieved what thousands of young footballers dream of when he played for his boyhood club, Inverness Caledonian Thistle, in the Scottish Premiership.

Yet the 31-year-old looks back on his career as proof of a difficult truth about youth development in Scotland.

Ferguson graduated from Caley Thistle's academy at 18 but played just two games for the first team before moving to lower league clubs and then to Canada and New Zealand to try to get top-flight football.

Now a development officer with Alba Football Alliance, he believes Scottish football continues to sell young players and their families the promise of a pathway from the academies to the first team, which for most will never be a reality.

"Parents believe their boy, or their girl, will get to the first team - that they will be a star in football," he told BBC Scotland's Eorpa programme.

"You just fall away from the game and your life changes overnight."

Calum now works as a development officer trying to bring through new talent

His comments come as Scottish football wrestles with a growing concern over the number of homegrown players who are making it to the top of the game.

In September, all 42 SPFL clubs gathered in St Andrews for a summit to discuss why so few young Scottish players are making the grade at elite level.

Data presented to the clubs showed that Scottish players under the age of 21 made up just 4.1% of minutes played in the Scottish Premiership.

By comparison, in the Danish Superliga, a league of the same size, the figure was 15.1%.

In the first round of fixtures in the Scottish Premiership this season, 28% of the starters were born in Scotland.

A stark contrast to similar sized Norway, where homegrown players made up 72% of the starting 11s on their opening weekend.

Nicklas Fuglestad regularly plays for Viking FK in Norway

This is because Norway has strict quotas.

Its league rules state that a club's full squad must include 16 homegrown players and a matchday squad can have a maximum of nine foreign players.

Nicklas Fuglestad is 20, and regularly plays for Viking FK, based in the Norwegian city of Stavanger. He believes quotas are good for the game.

"Everyone I know is very happy with how the Norwegian football league operates," he says.

"It makes it a bit easier for a young player to move up from the academy and make the step into A-league football."

Viking turned their focus to developing academy talent nearly a decade ago, after they were relegated to the second division.

After finishing champions last year, they have made it to the league stage of the Champions League, where they recently started eight Norwegians in their line-up, four of whom had been in their academy.

Another three from their academy came off the bench.

With both Viking FK and BodÃ¸/Glimt in Europe's top competition this year, it could be said that Norway is going through a golden generation.

Their national team reached the World Cup quarter final â and that wasn't just down to man mountain Erling Haaland.

Hakon Grottland says there is more to Norway's recent success than quotas

However, there's more to Norway's success than quotas, according to HÃ¥kon GrÃ¸ttland, head of player development at the Norwegian Football Federation.

He says two big changes over the past 25 years have made a huge difference - the increase in the use of artificial pitches, and more resources being put into coaching and talent development.

GrÃ¸ttland says artificial pitches allowed football to develop from a summer game to a year-round sport, turning Norway into a proper football nation.

Between 2016 and 2025 alone, 539 such pitches were built, with another 586 redeveloped.

Nearly all are open and free to use, so long as official games aren't taking place.

With Scottish football facing a talent crisis, Calum Maclennan examines the SFAâs youth development plans and discovers what Norwayâs successful system can teach Scotland.

GrÃ¸ttland says changes to player development have provided the second boost to the country's game.

"In the period 2010 to 2020 we used a lot of resources, hired a lot of talent coaches, and built some talent systems in Norway, where I think it's quite unique because it's a system that link grassroots football and top club football together," he says.

That talent system is Landslagskollen - or the National Team School (NTS) - that was established in 2013, following the country's failure to qualify for Euro 2012.

It's neither an academy nor a centralised school, but a national development structure connecting grassroots clubs, districts, top clubs and the federation.

Eleven of the 15 players who played in Norway's 2-1 win over Brazil in the round of 16 at this year's World Cup were part of the NTS pathway from under-15 or under-16s.

Despite a disappointing group campaign, a return to the World Cup after decades in the desert was a significant achievement for the Scotland national team.

The question now is whether the next generation can be developed.

The Tartan Army will not want to wait another 28 years.

Erling Haaland helped Norway to victory over Brazil in the World Cup this summer

At the meeting in St Andrews in September, the Scottish FA proposed quotas, as well as financial incentives, in an attempt to increase game time for young Scottish players.

The governing body put forward three suggestions:

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players to start in all Scottish Cup matches

Two under-21 Scotland-eligible players to start in all Premier Sports Cup matches

Clubs should field Scotland-eligible Under-21 players for an average of 60 minutes in each league game across all four SPFL divisions (6% of available minutes).

Two votes were to take place on the proposals.

The first, on the issue of Scottish Cup rule adoption, should have happened in October at the SFA's AGM, but did not take place.

The SFA now says it is expected to happen in mid-December.

The second vote is due to take place at the SPFL's annual meeting this month.

Adoption of the league and premier sports cup recommendations require 11 out of 12 top flight clubs to vote in favour â a high bar.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish said he wanted to give young players opportunities

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish told the BBC he did not believe the proposals went far enough â although he said he didn't think they would get voted through if they were more extreme.

"It's probably a little bit unfortunate, the governance in this country, that we can't just be told by one power, look this is what's happening," the 36-year-old said.

The young manager came into his role on an interim basis in March, before landing a permanent contract in the summer.

By the time BBC EÃ²rpa interviewed him in September, he'd given out six debuts to homegrown players.

Having worked in academy football for years, he says he could not sit where he is now and not give youngsters opportunities if they are ready.

A common argument against playing young players is the jeopardy that comes with managing in the Scottish Premiership.

Managers don't want to risk untried young players when they know that a handful of defeats could cost them their job.

"Yeah, you've got a longer term contract but you know that can be short-lived," Craig says.

"It's results based and I'm totally fine with that. I don't fear the negative outcome that can come.

Andrew Robertson and John McGinn both began their careers in the Scottish youth system

In recent years, top players such as Andrew Robertson, John McGinn, and Ryan Christie, have all had a significant grounding in the Scottish Premiership before moving on to greater things.

And regardless of talent coaches or quotas for homegrown players, the Scottish top flight can be extremely entertaining.

That much was clear last season, when fans were treated to the most enticing title race in years.

It is now up to the clubs to decide whether they want their league to be more Scottish.

All will become clear once the votes on the SFA's proposals take place.

Although the delay would suggest things are not going as the governing body would have liked.

Will Scottish football finally agree on how to fix youth development?

#811. Worst in the EFL - the team with a penalty problem

Shaquille Gwengwe is among several Newport players to miss from the penalty spot

While fans would normally celebrate their team earning a penalty, Newport County supporters could be forgiven for putting their heads in their hands.

With three-quarters of penalties successfully converted, on average, earning a spot kick would normally be reason to celebrate.

Not so for Newport where anticipation has been replaced by apprehension.

Across the past two seasons, they have converted just two of nine penalties in all competitions - and only one of six in League Two.

Their 16.7% conversion rate is the worst in the entire English Football League (EFL).

And for a team just two points off the play-offs, missed penalties could prove costly.

Three different managers and several players have tried to find the formula, but the outcome has remained remarkably similar.

There was hope Harrison Biggins had ended the slump when he netted from the spot in a draw at Rotherham in October.

Four days later, that optimism evaporated.

The midfielder stepped up against Cheltenham Town but, having chosen the same side, saw his effort saved in the 1-0 defeat.

Manager Hayden Mullins refused to blame Biggins after his miss at Cheltenham and, having done the job himself as a player, has sympathy.

"We never lay any blame on anyone who steps up to take a penalty," said the 47-year-old.

"Penalties are always tough. Harrison scored the game before [but] it's a game of cat and mouse really between you and the goalkeeper.

"You don't know what the goalkeeper is thinking, all you can do is pick a side and execute it with aggression."

Dibley-Dias to miss County's game against Chesterfield

Exiles' Mullins not given enough credit - Jenkins

While a player may not be able to predict a goalkeeper's thought process, recent penalties may have handed Stanway a clue.

Six of Newport's last nine penalties have been aimed to the right and - on each occasion - the keeper has guessed correctly with Cameron Antwi, Nathaniel Opoku, Bobby Kamwa and Shaquille Gwengwe all denied. Only Biggins' effort at Rotherham found the net.

Even when Newport altered their approach, the result was often no different.

Ged Garner was denied to the left against Swindon Town and Yahya Bamba - aiming for the top corner - saw his effort ruled out for a double touch.

Bamba converted the retake by waiting for the goalkeeper to move, a method similar to manager Mullins' own approach during his midfield days with Crystal Palace, West Ham and Portsmouth.

"I know how hard it is. Everyone's got their own technique," said Mullins.

"I would run up, have one eye on the goalkeeper and whichever way he went, I would go the other way, but it's brave."

Newport County have the worst conversion rate from the spot in the entire EFL

It begs the question whether or not Newport practice penalties.

They have not always struggled from the spot and between 2023 and 2025, scored 10 of 13 between forwards Will Evans and Omar Bogle.

Mullins prefers to hand sole responsibility to to his centre-forward but has been without Shaquille Gwenge through suspension for the past three games - during which Newport have missed two penalties - since missing from the spot himself.

Gwenge is available again and Mullins insisted the striker - with six goals already this season - practices penalties "for a long time" after training.

But the County boss says he would "never spend too much energy" worrying about the miserable success rate.

"Penalties are down to a lot of things - fatigue, mindset, where you are, who you're taking it in front of, how you feel at that time and who you're up against," he said.

"We can look at it and practice as much as we can.

"We'll be ready for the next time we take it and hopefully it goes our way."
