#810. Tyler Baltierra & Catelynn Lowell Aren't the Only Happy Teen Mom Pair

While Catelynn Lowell and Tyler Baltierra have been committed since middle school, some Teen Mom costars are still enjoying that first blush of romance. We promise you'll, uh, love this round-up.

More than two decades into their relationship, Tyler Baltierra is quite grateful to still be under Catelynn Lowell's spell.

And with his bride of 11 years having spent the past few months brewing up something special, he treated her to some well-earned Halloween praise.

"Can we just take a moment to acknowledge how beautiful my wife is!?" he captioned a Nov. 1 Instagram showcasing Lowell in her witch costume from 2025 and 2026. "She's down 30lbs & I’m so beyond proud of her!"

Having undergone his own health journey in 2018, game recognizes game. But, of course, Baltierra added, "You're always the most beautiful to me!"

Once 16 and Pregnant, the franchises longest-running pair are now 34 and settled with daughters Nova, 11, Vaeda, 7, and Rya, 4.

"If I could go back & do it all over again…I’d only change one thing," Baltierra noted in an Oct. 7 Instagram tribute to his middle school sweetheart. "I'd go back further in time from when we first met & find you sooner, so l could love you longer!"

The sentiment echoed Lowell's 2025 post assuring him, "I will love you for this whole lifetime.. and in every life after this one!!!"

Of course, the Michigan-based duo—who placed eldest daughter Carly for adoption in 2009—aren't the only Teen Mom stars who are confident they've found their person.

"I want to be a wife one day," Kailyn Lowry recently explained to E! News of laying out her expectations for boyfriend Isaac "Ike" Knighton early into their 18-month romance. Wanting to have a ring on her finger before their second anniversary this spring, she acknowledged, "Not everyone is on my timeline. But this is what I want."

Judging by how Knighton has seamlessly fit into her life with Elliott (Lowry's 16-year-old son with ex Jo Rivera), Lincoln (she shares the 12-year-old with former husband Javi Marroquin), Lux, 9, Creed, 6 (her sons with ex Chris Lopez), Rio, 4, and 3-year-old twins Verse and Valley (with Lowry's ex-fiancé Elijah Scott), he's on the same calendar page.

Because if he wasn't interested in following through on creating her dream ring, Lowry noted, "I would question why he's doing all of the other husband-type things."

With cuffing season upon us, she's not alone in locking things down, with Amber Portwood calling her boyfriend of nearly a year, "my anchor."

So, we dove deep to see which Teen Mom romances are enjoying smooth sailing and those that have navigated some rough waters.

Viewers watched Catelynn Lowell and now-husband Tyler Baltierra make the difficult choice to place their first daughter, Carly, for adoption, in 2009 on the inaugural season of 16 and Pregnant. After 13 years together, the fan-favorite couple wed in August 2015 and have since had three more daughters: Novalee, Vaeda and Rya.

While the absence of Carly—who lives with her adoptive parents, Brandon and Teresa Davis—still aches, the couple keep fighting for a future.

Their hope is their bond "is whatever she wants," Catelynn told E! News in January 2025. "Whether she just wants a relationship with her biological siblings, if she wants to have a relationship with us, awesome. If she doesn't, totally understand. Whatever that looks like for her. Because it needs to be adoptee-centered."

Together less than six months when she got pregnant, viewers saw Maci Bookout struggle with an irresponsible Ryan Edwards on 16 and Pregnant. Though they got engaged, the high school sweethearts split less than a year after their son Bentley was born in 2008.

These days they're focused on building a co-parenting relationship. "We're in a good place," Maci revealed to E! News in 2023, adding that Ryan is showing up "more consistently now than maybe he ever has before."

Maci found her forever teammate in Texan Taylor McKinney in 2012 and the pair soon began building up their squad. They welcomed daughter Jayde in May 2015 and son Maverick a year later, then wed in Florida that October.

Partners in parenting, life and their TTM Lifestyle fashion brand, "He's just my person," she told E! News in 2023. "Even when we've had a rough year together, I think at the end of the day, I still choose him. I like him. And even if I want to punch him in the face sometimes, I'd rather argue with him or have a rough patch with him than never have a rough patch with anybody else."

Despite moving on with new significant others, the MTV stars, who connected while filming The Challenge, continue to co-parent their daughter Ryder together.

"Our biggest thing since day one of Cory coming into Ryder's life was what kind of dad he wanted to be and what kind of parent he wanted to be," Cheyenne explained to E! News in March 2020. "I wasn't going to allow him to be a Disneyland dad or an Instagram dad or just in the moment. He had to be 100 percent. I think from the beginning, he saw my mindset and appreciated it so that's why we co-parent so well."

After their romance ended in 2018, the pair decided to give their relationship a second chance. While celebrating her 28th birthday, Cheyenne confirmed on Instagram that she was back with Zach. In May 2021, the couple welcomed their first child together, son Ace, and got married in September 2022.

"We spent the past two years knocking things off our list," Cheyenne told E! News in 2024. "We wanted to have a baby, we had Ace. We wanted to get married, we had our wedding. We wanted to buy a house, we bought our house."

And now, she continued, "I don't want to do anything. I don't want to set a goal. I want to sit down. I want to be really still. My goal is to be still and just to be happy with where we're at. And just to like each other. That's it. I want nothing else."

Well...maybe a little something. Cheyenne announced she was expecting her third child on a May 2025 episode of Teen Mom: The Next Chapter.

"We definitely kind of teetered back and forth on wanting a baby," Zach told Us Weekly ahead of welcoming son Saint in December 2025. "I wanted one, and then she went through the phase of wanting one, and I wasn’t on the same page as her, but then we kind of came to the same chapter, and we tried to make it work."

Connecting while filming Ex on the Beach may not sound like the start of a love story, but Cory and Are You the One? alum Taylor Selfridge—who shared Mila and Maya—enjoyed years of sunny skies.

"We just bought a house," he shared with E! News in 2023, before bringing up that, yes, he's aware that people want to know when they're getting married. "It's definitely being talked about. We have everything but the ring and me just letting her know. Taylor deserves that and it's something that I want and she wants. Right now we're just taking steps to get there."

Unfortunately, they experienced a few stumbles, confirming their breakup in October 2026, shortly after he was seen flirting with fellow competitor Izzy Fairthorne on the 42nd season of The Challenge.

"We had our issues before this season," Cory acknowledged to E! News. "We really did. But I didn't mean to disrespect her. I just shouldn't have been so selfish."

Testing the limits of for-better-or-for-worse, Ryan checked into rehab not long after he married Mackenzie Standifer in May 2017, with her giving birth to their first son Jagger in 2018 while Ryan was still in treatment.

Though the pair would welcome daughter Stella in January 2020, Mackenzie filed for divorce three years later.

Following his breakup with Mackenzie, Ryan started dating Amanda in 2023. He popped the question the following year during a family vacation.

The pair welcomed daughter Presley in February 2025, seven months before announcing their marriage.

An October 2026 issue that saw Amanda accuse him of cheating, proved to just be a hurdle. "We've been dealing with this for a long time," she explained in a TikTok. "Somebody has been giving Ryan’s number out and putting them in this escort website and these women call and text his phone, send him pictures."

While their very contentious romance came to an end for good in 2013, the couple managed to co-parent their now-teenage daughter Leah for years.

"We have fun together but at a distance," Amber told E! News in January 2022. "But our relationship is good. It's a family now so we treat it as a family more than anything else."

Though, of course, sometimes families fight. In recent years, Amber has taken to social media with enough claims about Gary to suggest they're no longer the friendliest of exes and her growing rift with Leah has been showcased on Teen Mom: The Next Chapter.

After several years together, a proposal and one unsuccessful stint on Marriage Boot Camp, Amber and Boston transplant Matt Baier called off their engagement in 2017.

"Honestly, you just get to a point when you're done hearing things and you just start to not care in a relationship and I think that's what started happening to me and him," Amber revealed on Dr. Drew Pinsky's podcast later that year. "I started not to care anymore about the relationship like you should. I put a wall up so I wouldn't get hurt again pretty much."

Amber did find love while filming Marriage Boot Camp—connecting with crew member Andrew Glennon while on set. The pair made their debut as a couple at the 2017 MTV Movie Awards and in May 2018, Amber gave birth to the couple's son, James.

But the couple separated not long after Amber was arrested for domestic battery in July 2019. And after a contentious court battle, California native Andrew was awarded sole legal and primary physical custody of their son in 2022.

"I've worked so hard to better myself and improve my relationships with my children," the Teen Mom star told E! News at the time. "While I've always been candid about my past substance abuse and struggles with mental illness, a person should have the chance to redeem themselves and not be tethered to their problems from the past."

Determined not to give up, she added, "If your road has not been perfect, but you've worked hard to become a better, more stable and caring person today, keep moving forward as I will. I'll never stop fighting for my children who I love more than anything."

After meeting Amber on the Internet, Dimitri Garcia made his Teen Mom OG debut in April 2020. "Dimitri is from Belgium. He's 39 so he's 10 years older than me. But he's a very handsome man," Amber shared on the show. "I started opening up to him and we decided we should meet since we like each other."

In April 2021, Amber revealed on the Teen Mom OG reunion special that she was still dating Dimitri. "We've known each other now for 18 months," she explained. "But I haven't seen him in a year though." Though the pair never officially announced a split, Amber introduced new flame Gary Wayt during a June 2024 episode of Teen Mom: The Next Chapter.

After Amber connected with Gary 2.0 on a dating app in the fall of 2023, he zoomed into the picture when the Teen Mom vet introduced him to her castmates during a virtual chat.

Though he proposed in May 2024, their betrothal was short-lived. While in North Carolina for her brother's wedding that June, Gary ran off after the pair had a fight, leading Amber to report him as missing.

And while Gary was soon located, the duo's engagment wasn't the only thing left broken.

"I've had to deal with thinking my fiancé was dead for three to four days," Amber said on Teen Mom: The Next Chapter. "I had to deal with literally grieving and trying to make sense of why the f--k would somebody do this to me. I am going through something right now."

"This man broke me," she continued. "I was stable. Right now, this is the first time in years in my life I am not f--king right because a man put a ring on my finger."

Meeting her current boyfriend in the spring of 2025 helped jump start the healing. "He's my anchor," she raved in an October 2026 YouTube video. "He's very calm. Comes from a very sweet Catholic family. They don't cuss. They don't do stuff like that."

Months after Gary and now-wife Kristina Anderson welcomed daughter Emilee in April 2015, they wed in a sweet beach ceremony.

"You are one of the most beautiful souls I know," Gary wrote in a 2022 Instagram post. "I don’t know how I would do this without you."

The father of Farrah Abraham's daughter Sophia died in an accident two months prior to her birth in December 2008.

For her first serious relationship since the death of her high school boyfriend, Farrah dated real estate agent Simon Saran on and off for over two years.

Though their 2017 split got ugly (as in cease-and-desist ugly), the two gave a stab at trying to remain friends. Sorta.

"I have no hard feelings against Farrah," Simon told E! News at the time. "We are just from two different worlds. She likes the fake life, I want what's real. I wish the best for her and much success in all of her future endeavors."

Jenelle Evans and Andrew Lewis, parents to now-teenage Jace, split not long after his 2009 birth, with the model having little involvement in his son's life.

“I do feel bad because that’s Jace's dad," Jenelle reflected on a 2019 episode of Teen Mom 2. "But I know how he is, and I don’t want him to disappoint my son. I don’t want [him] to pop back in and then pop back out."

After a one-year marriage to Courtland Rogers, and having her second child, Kaiser, with ex-fiancé Nathan Griffin in 2014, Jenelle wed David Eason on their North Carolina property in September 2017, eight months after they welcomed their daughter Ensley.

After a particularly rocky stretch saw David charged with a child abuse misdemeanor involving Jace (at the time, Jenelle likened it to a "smear campaign"), Jenelle revealed they had separated.

"I would've skipped straight to divorce but I couldn't because in the state of North Carolina, you have to be legally separated for a year," she explained on social media, "and you have to prove you have two separate addresses."

Their divorce was finalized in July 2025.

Remember the charmer who asked then-girlfriend Chelsea Houska when he could "sign the papers over for that mistake"?

Against all odds, the Teen Mom star-turned-HGTV personality has a somewhat copacetic relationship with her high school ex Adam Lind, mom to her eldest daughter Aubree. “There’s no bad vibes and it’s just a very open relationship," she told Us Weekly. "There’s no bad feelings. We see him sometimes and it’s totally fine."

What began as a meet-cute at a gas station in 2014 became forever when Chelsea and Cole DeBoer wed in October 2016. After welcoming son Watson in 2017 and daughters Layne and Walker in 2018 and 2021, respectively, the pair launched a new joint project: Their HGTV series Down Home Fab.

"If we were going to come back to TV, I wanted it to be something lighthearted, feel good and be able to show our authentic selves," Chelsea explained to E! News, sharing why this move felt "so right." As she put it, "This was just such a cool opportunity to do that."

As for whether they're planning any more additions, "I have so many friends who are like, 'We are done,' and they just have that feeling," Chelsea told E! in June 2025. "And I don't know if I'll ever have that feeling."

Though then-high schooler Leah Messer and Corey Simms fought to turn their friendship into a forever family, the parents to now-teenage twins Aleeah and Aliannah filed for divorce six months after their October 2010 wedding.

Corey has been married to Miranda Patterson since 2013.

Leah went on to wed pipeliner Jeremy Calvert in 2012, the couple welcoming daughter Adalynn the next year.

Though they split in 2015, they have made an effort to co-parent their daughter with sometimes mixed results.

"I'm looking at a complete, better version of myself," Leah told E! News of her girls. "And seeing everything that they love and enjoy doing, and being able to support them in their lives and be a part of it is magical. I love it. I love being a mom, especially a girl mama."

By the time Leah went Instagram official with Jaylan Mobley in 2021, the United States Army officer had already charmed her and her daughters.

The couple announced their engagement in August 2022, but broke up that October.

"I needed that breakup," the Teen Mom star confessed to E! News a year later. "I've learned a lot from my last breakup and, moving forward, I do feel like my life is just beginning."

Kailyn Lowry was just 17 when she and high school boyfriend Jo Rivera welcomed their eldest son, Isaac, in 2010.

And though they split a year later, they've since settled into a comfortable co-parenting arrangement, Kailyn even hosting her now-canceled Baby Mamas No Drama podcast with Jo's wife Vee Torres for years. "We’ve come a long way since we were 18," Kailyn wrote on X after attending Jo and Vee's 2018 wedding. "I couldn’t ask for a better stepmom for isaac."

Kailyn's second son Lincoln joined the squad in November 2013, roughly a year after the then-star of Teen Mom 2 wed his father Javi Marroquin.

Splitting in late 2016, the former spouses have had an, at times, rocky relationship as they've each moved on.

While Kail moved on to Elijah Scott, Javi wed Lauren Comeau at an intimate ceremony on Florida's Vero Beach in April 2025. "Only my dad, our kids & pastor were there," Lauren wrote on Instagram Stories of son Eli and daughter Maizee. "We have a reception planned for this summer with family and friends. They were fully supportive of this & Jav's mom has got to experience his firsts already so there was no issues. We wanted it to be something special for the boys, and something intimate for our family, and for my dad to walk me down the aisle."

Months after their June 2025 beach bash, the newlyweds announced they were expecting their third child together. "The best honeymoon souvenir," Javi wrote on Instagram in August 2025. "So grateful to be doing this again with you momma! You’re the strongest woman I know and we are beyond lucky."

They welcomed son Cooper in March 2026, calling him, "The sweetest grand finale."

Though Kailyn welcomed sons Lux and Creed with Chris during their on-and-off romance, they eventually called it quits for good.

"Right now, we don't communicate at all," she revealed to E! News in 2020. "I'm hoping that it will get better with time but I don't have a big vision. I don't have anything negative to say. I hope for our kids that everything works itself out in whatever direction that may be."

With construction worker Elijah, Kailyn felt she had finally built that strong foundation. "It's been very different from my other partners and my kids' other dads," she told People of Elijah, dad to her son Rio and twins Verse and Valley. "He pours concrete, he gets down and dirty at work. But he's also just a real family man. He's very, very much connected with his own family, with our family, and so he's been a really good partner to me, and I feel like it's a really good match."

A strong enough one that she finally said yes to one of his many proposals, in fact.

"He asked me to marry him several times and I never said no," Kailyn insisted to E! News in September 2024 of her neighbor-turned-life partner. "I was just like, 'Yes, but not right now.'"

Ultimately, though, the timing wasn't right, Kailyn revealing in July 2025 that they had split.

"I get a lot of s--t for leaving my kids' dads,” she detailed on the Give them Lala podcast. "I left all of them because I, to some degree, take no s--t."

Despite having known Ike "since pretty much high school," Kailyn said things didn't turn romantic until 2025 following her breakup with Elijah.

“I don’t think I expected to have a full-blown relationship," she shared in a January 2026 Patreon video, "but after the first time we hung out, both of us just knew what it was."

Ike moved in with Kailyn soon after, a decision she admitted can seem "selfish" to her kids at first.

"You cannot deny chemistry and attraction when it’s there,” she argued. "If I'm not happy as a woman first, I cannot be a good mom. And I’m not saying I’m relying on men for happiness because—if we are being honest and you look at my track record—they have all made me miserable."

But she's confident she's found herself a winner. "My kids love him," she raved to E! News in October 2026. "You would think seven kids is so chaotic that how could anyone take this on? But he fit right in."

Though Indiana-based Jade Cline and Sean Austin had more than their share of ups and down since welcoming daughter Kloie in 2017, in January 2022 Jade teased to fans that they were on the rise.

"There were some major, major things that happened with our lives and major improvements that happen with Sean's life as well and with his future," she told E! News. "I'm really proud of him and where we are today." Eight months later, the pair announced their engagement, marrying in October 2023.

"I know for sure my relationship isn't always perfect," Jade told E! News in 2024. "But we love each other and we make it work."

California natives Ashley Jones and Bar Smith privately wed in 2021—four years after they welcomed daughter Holly.

But after calling off their romance several times, Ashley officially filed for divorce in 2024.

#809. Serbia: Hope, tension and apprehension as voters prepare to elect new parliament

After two years of protests, Serbia faces a pivotal election on Sunday, with a student-led challenge to Aleksandar Vucic's lengthy rule. Allegations of electoral irregularities and fears of a post-election crisis abound.

A sense of hope swept through Belgrade on Thursday evening as thousands gathered for the final rally of the Student List, the group of candidates put forward by the student movement that has been protesting against the government for almost exactly two years.

The Student List is calling for an end to the current regime in Serbia via the ballot box in Sunday's parliamentary election.

Many of those who attended the rally had spent days walking to the Serbian capital from all four corners of the country, turning the campaign finale into a display of solidarity and peaceful determination.

"We have walked across Serbia from one end to the other, visited villages and neighborhoods, looked you in the eye and realized that we can count on you," biology student Arsa Stojanovic told the crowd.

"People, it smells like freedom," added Aleksandar Cupic, professor of transport and traffic engineering, and a candidate on the Student List.

After 24 months of protests sparked by the collapse of a concrete canopy at Novi Sad railway station, which killed 16 people in November 2024, Serbia is heading into an election unlike any other in the 14 years since the Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) first came to power.

For the first time in years, the ruling party faces a serious political challenge, which this time comes from a student movement that has channeled widespread public discontent into an electoral campaign.

"These are the first elections since [Aleksandar] Vucic came to power in 2012 that are competitive and whose outcome is uncertain," political scientist Dusan Spasojevic told DW. "The student movement has generated hope among citizens and substantial support. Polls suggest that they could even win more than 40% of the vote."

The Student List has framed the election as a chance to confront corruption and demand accountability for a disaster that became a symbol of institutional failure.

In doing so, the students have sought to put aside the ideological, social and foreign-policy divisions that have long shaped Serbian politics.

Just a few kilometers away, also in Belgrade, the ruling SNS held its own final rally.

The message here was familiar: A vote for the SNS means stability, continuity and further prosperity, while a change of government would risk plunging the country into chaos.

The party framed the election as a battle for Serbia's future and sovereignty, accusing its opponents of serving foreign interests.

"They tried to destroy our country on foreign orders, and that is why this is the hardest battle," former President Aleksandar Vucic told his supporters. "They attacked us with billions of euros, and we defended ourselves with integrity, our program, love for our homeland and Serbia's achievements."

The campaign has increasingly been overshadowed by violence, reflecting a society in which political opponents are often portrayed not simply as rivals, but as enemies.

By the final week of the campaign, CRTA, an independent election-monitoring organization, had recorded 116 incidents involving physical violence or verbal threats. The incidents included physical confrontations, attacks on campaigners and attempts to seize campaign banners.

CRTA also reported that opposition activists, particularly those linked to the Student List, were also subjected to surveillance  and police questioning. In some cases, the organization said, police were slow to protect opposition candidates and supporters.

In the final runup to the election, there have also been a series of investigative reports examining alleged links between people connected to the ruling SNS and criminal networks.

Published by independent media in the days before the election, the reports have brought renewed attention to questions of corruption, political influence and accountability — issues at the heart of the student movement's challenge to the government.

But Spasojevic is skeptical that the revelations will make a significant difference to the election outcome.

He argues that those who trust investigative media are likely to have already made up their minds, while voters who rely on pro-government outlets may never even see these reports.

There are also serious concerns about the fairness of the election process.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

CRTA told DW that the election campaign has not been either free or fair from day one, citing "a narrowing of freedoms and deepening inequality" among candidates and voters.

Its report found a pronounced imbalance in media coverage: Almost three-quarters of airtime devoted to political players on national television has featured government representatives, while more than 80% of coverage on the Student List has been negative.

Ahead of the vote, the Balkan Investigative Reporting Network (BIRN) published the testimony of a former member of the SNS, who described how public-sector employees were pressured to deliver votes for the party.

DW has also learned from sources who want to remain anonymous that voters have been offered between €30 and €150 to vote for the SNS, with holiday packages reportedly offered to entire families if they pledge all their votes to the ruling party.

Many fear a period of turbulence, uncertainty and political crisis after the vote, with election night itself a particular source of anxiety.

For weeks, the authorities have warned that students, allegedly with the help of foreign intelligence services, are preparing violence in the streets. In the final days of the campaign, several people were arrested on what the prosecution has said was the suspicion of plotting disturbances on election night.

The best-case scenario, says Dusan Spasojevic, would be a decisive victory for one of the two opposing camps, leaving little room for the other to challenge the result.

"But polls suggest that the margin will be narrow, and we will probably enter some kind of post-election crisis," he said, adding that a narrow victory for the ruling party would almost certainly be contested, given longstanding concerns about the fairness of the electoral process and allegations that some votes may have been obtained illegally.

Whatever happens, the European Union's response could be crucial.

"I think the international response will be crucial in preventing major incidents and a further escalation of the crisis. It is the only thing that can persuade the authorities to accept defeat and refrain from an overly heavy-handed response to any protests or incidents," he told DW.

An EU Commission spokesperson acknowledged to DW that key recommendations on improving Serbia's electoral framework remain unimplemented and also stressed that democracy and the rule of law are key to the accession process. Serbia has been an EU candidate country since 2012.

Back in Belgrade, the students ended their rally with a kolo, a traditional Serbian circle dance, projecting confidence in their chances at the ballot box.

But the path to victory could prove difficult. The movement has vowed to defend every vote — setting the stage for a potentially tense election night if the results are disputed.

#808. Are Celtic club in regression amid run of six defeats in 10?

Celtic dropped points for the second game running

Towards the end of Sunday's Scottish Premiership defeat by Falkirk, Chris Sutton said it was looking like "one of those days" for Celtic. Afterwards, his remarks about Martin O'Neill's side were much more pointed.

"Martin's not going to say it, of course, but the club is in regression, the team is in regression," Sutton stated on Sky Sports.

"They're just not a good functioning team at this moment in time. It's hard to see how Celtic are actually set up and it is a bit off the cuff.

"They're deficient in every area of the team. This current team are miles off it. Where is the plan, what's the strategy?"

There was some mitigation in the leader leaders' surprise defeat on Sunday - their sixth in 10 matches in all competitions.

Goalkeeper Scott Bain excelled in goal for Falkirk against his former club - as O'Neill acknowledged - and Falkirk dug in when they needed to get over the line.

Impressive Falkirk earn first win over hapless Celtic in 19 years

Latest Celtic news, analysis and fan views

They are still four points clear, but some other stats paint a grim picture for Celtic.

Twenty-four shots to Falkirk's six; nine on target compared to Falkirk's two (their two goals); more than double the possession and almost three times as many touches in the opposition box. Celtic had 14 corners, Falkirk had none.

Former Falkirk manager Ian McCall was in accord with Sutton, and former Rangers striker Kris Boyd, who said he "couldn't see what Celtic were trying to do".

McCall pointed to age and injury taking its toll on on previously peerless performers. "Carter-Vickers, Tierney, McGregor, Forrest - all of them for different reasons aren't quite what they were," he said on Sportsound.

"That happens in football, it's cruel. Whether it's injury or overuse in Callum McGregor's case, I would suggest. Their bodies maybe aren't capable of the levels they once were.

Europe aside, Celtic's season had been rattling along relatively well.

They had bounced back from League Cup and league losses to Rangers with a solid win at Motherwell, a resounding 7-1 victory at home to last season's runners-up Hearts, and a hard-fought 2-1 win from behind at Hibernian.

Wednesday's 2-2 draw with Dundee United turned out to be a missed opportunity to extend their lead at the top and they now face the prospect of Rangers and, indeed, Hearts getting closer should they win their games in hand.

Besiktas in the Europa League are next up, a home game Celtic really need to win to stand any chance of progress in that competition after starting with three defeats.

Former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner said of O'Neill on BBC Radio Scotland that it's been "a brilliant weekend for Rangers", who won their League Cup semi-final with Aberdeen on Saturday.

"They're in the cup final and Celtic getting beat allows them, when they play their game, their extra game, to close the gap.

"That then puts huge pressure on to Celtic with the European game coming up now in midweek also. That is going to be tough for them to bounce back from this."

'We were in a worse position last year' - O'Neill on Falkirk loss

Of course, O'Neill has seen this all before - fairly recently, in fact. He twice stepped back into the dugout in Celtic's hour of need last season and ultimately led them to a league and cup double.

Indeed, sitting atop the Premiership after 12 games, he was quick to point out in his spiky post-match interview that Celtic are in a better position than at the same stage last season, when they were four points behind leaders Hearts.

"I don't know whether [supporters] are angry," O'Neill told BBC Sport Scotland. "Every single time that Celtic lose a game, people can be angry and frustrated. We come under scrutiny and so we should because this is it, the club is used to winning.

"It's a long season. This time last year, we were in a worse position."

O'Neill was also asked about the amount of changes that had been made to his team of late.

"Why would you not change the team? We have an abundance of games," he replied.

"We're playing European football. We're trying to hold the Scottish flag up, so we have to change. It's hard for the same players to play every single week."

Alan: Sorry to say, but the plot has been lost. Strange bench selection. Even stranger half-time sub. Then we take off our best two midfielders and leave an underperforming captain on the pitch. What is going on??

Imran: I think football has changed too much for O'Neill to be a modern manager. I think he should take a back seat and allow a younger, more ambitious manager to take charge. It would be a shame for his legacy to be tarnished and that's what looks like will happen as no major changes look imminent.

Sean: Very, very Poor. Falkirk deserved the win.

Kevin: Keep the faith Celtic fans... stay strong.

Edward: Dismal display, Johnstone is not in any way superior to Sinisalo, was surprised at Carter-Vickers performance. The unthinkable must now be thought. Is Martin O'Neill able to progress this side? If the answer was Forrest, Tounekti and McCowan the question is NOT how to win a football match.

Liam: Enough is enough. This is rapidly turning into a disaster and we need change: from the board to the manager to the coaching staff to the players. So much for quality over quantity.

#807. Adam Driver Jokingly Shares Parenting Rule: "I’m Not Giving Him S--t"

Paper Tiger star Adam Driver exclusively revealed to E! News how he's navigating raising kids in Hollywood, especially as he finds they are more privileged than he was growing up.

Adam Driver’s life in Hollywood has awoken a new parenting technique.

The Oscar nominee revealed that he and wife Joanne Tucker are careful with how they’re raising their son and daughter, especially because their kids already “have more growing up” than they had.

“I don't want to get too caught in the, ‘You don't realize what you have,’” Driver exclusively shared with E! News in a joint interview with Paper Tiger costar Scarlett Johansson, “because that's kind of wasted energy. It is what it is—[they] have more privilege than I had.”

While the 42-year-old noted that overall “that's a good thing,” he also feared it “could also be a trap where things are taken for granted”—especially when he thought about his son.

“I try to make sure that he understands where everything comes from and that he has to work for it to get it,” Driver said, quipping, “and I'm not giving him s--t.”

For now, the biggest lesson the Star Wars actor hoped to impart on his son was to always “make sure that he has manners.”

“Manners is a big thing in our house. It's kind of a baseline thing that is very massive,” he shared. “I think it's very important. You have to have respect with every people, no matter where they are.”

And while his 3-year-old daughter is still figuring out how to mind her p’s and q’s, his son is already “very good” with them.

Wanting better for your children is also a subject he and Johansson touch on in Paper Tiger, which follows the story of two brothers played by Driver and Miles Teller who attempt to pursue lucrative business opportunities only to find themselves entangled with the Russian mafia.

The film also served as a reunion for Driver and Johansson after playing husband and wife in 2019’s Marriage Story. And Johansson was thrilled to work alongside Driver again.

“We like to be on the set hanging out and working together,” she shared with E! News. “When you have somebody that you love their work, you love the act of working with them, you love to watch them work, you're excited to see what they're gonna do with something.”

Paper Tiger hits select theaters Nov. 13 before releasing in theaters nationwide Nov. 20.

#806. Patrick Stewart dies: how Captain Picard inspired today’s science leaders

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Actor Patrick Stewart as Captain Jean-Luc Picard.Credit: RGR Collection/Alamy

Researchers have joined the chorus of Star Trek fans expressing grief at the death of actor Patrick Stewart, who played the legendary Captain Jean-Luc Picard.

Stewart, who died on 28 October aged 86, portrayed Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation from 1987 to 1994 and in various films from the franchise. As captain of the starship USS Enterprise, Picard led his crew on an intergalactic exploration in the twenty-fourth century as they encountered new worlds and civilizations. For many scientists, Captain Picard exemplified the qualities of a good scientific leader.

“His first immediate thought was to consider all angles and to ask questions,” says Sarah Bickerton, a public-policy researcher at the University of Auckland in New Zealand. But more importantly, says Bickerton, Picard consulted his Enterprise crew members — irrespective of rank — before making decisions. That shaped Bickerton’s own leadership approach. She says she makes a point of consulting her research assistants and graduate students on important decisions.

A film from the franchise that had an impact on Bickerton was Star Trek: First Contact (1996), in which Picard travels back in time to the twenty-first century and explains that in the future, money does not exist. “We work to better ourselves and the rest of humanity,” Picard says.

Bickerton says: “For scientists, that really resonates. What drives us is bettering ourselves and the rest of humanity through the search for knowledge and just to learn and understand.”

Other researchers have also been inspired by Picard’s style of leadership. In a 2025 interview with Kentucky Alumni magazine, Tracy Drain, a flight systems engineer at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena, California, said that she loved how the character modelled what an excellent leader could be. “He was even-keeled, respectful, kind to everyone,” she said. “He encouraged his crew to think outside the box and supported them in what they needed to do.”

On social media, scientists expressed how the character of Picard influenced their scientific careers.

Jordan Harrison, a psychologist in Ann Arbor, Michigan, wrote on Bluesky: “I can trace my initial interest in science, my love of space and astronomy, the seeds of an ethic of care for others different than me, and early memories of bonding with my dad over pop culture to Star Trek: TNG and Patrick Stewart’s portrayal of Captain Jean-Luc Picard. This one hurts.”

Ariana Grande and boyfriend Ricky Álvarez, who she first dated in 2015, continued to show off their rekindled romance in the Focker-In-Law's Nov. 2 Instagram dump.

Ariana Grande and Ricky Álvarez are putting their tattooed hearts on display.

The couple—who first dated from 2015 to 2016—continued to flaunt their love on social media months after sparking rumors that they'd rekindled their romance.

Grande led her Nov. 2 Instagram carousel post with a photo of her lovingly embracing Álvarez as they made intimate eye contact with one another.

In the picture taken from below, the "Be Alright" singer stands on her tip-toes in an off-white raincoat, dark wide-legged pants and white kitten heels as she wraps her arms around her boyfriend. Meanwhile, he's smiling in a beanie, green sweater and dark pants.

Grande also included a dimly-lit selfie in the dump in which she kisses Álvarez on the forehead as he closes his eyes.

The Fockers-In-Law star—who also showed off her new flipped bob hairdo in several pictures—first confirmed her reconciliation with the backup dancer by making it Instagram official back in August. However, changes that she'd made to the lyrics of her song "thank u, next" while performing it during her Eternal Sunshine tour throughout the summer were what first stoked rumors her and Álvarez’s friendship had once more blossomed into romance.

Instead of singing, "Wrote some songs about Ricky / Now I listen and laugh," the 33-year-old reworked the line into "Wrote some songs about Ricky / I’m tryna make him my last," "And they still really slap," "I know he still got my back" and, perhaps most tellingly, "We’ll always find our way back."

The Oscar nominee—who split from Wicked costar Ethan Slater earlier this year, E! News confirmed in June—further got fans talking when she shared a picture on her Instagram Stories Aug. 15 of a new script lettering tattoo on her collarbone that read “I do love you,” which Arianators realized matched has the same words tattooed on Álvarez's collarbone (though his is in a different font).

And, actually, Álvarez included a photo of Grande's tattoo in an Instagram dump of his own shared back on Sept. 26, which also featured a mirror selfie of the "Into You" singer giving him a kiss on the lips.

Keep reading for more about Grande's dating history...

Though Ariana Grande and actor Graham Phillips have since gone their separate ways, the pair have proved they certainly can be friends.

The Grammy winner and The Good Wife alum met in 2008 while starring in the hit Broadway musical 13.

And while the duo may have called it quits in 2011, it’s obvious they’ve remained on good terms, sharing a selfie from a “Lil 13 reunion” they had in 2016 and enjoying a 2019 dinner together in New York.

While it’s a true story that Jai Brooks dated Grande for nearly two years, their on-again off-again relationship wasn’t always full of sweetener.

Indeed, the Australian YouTuber shot his shot with Grande over X (formerly Twitter) in 2012 as part of a challenge with twin brother Luke Brooks. The siblings—part of YouTube comedy group The Janoskians—competed to see who could get the Nickelodeon star’s attention first.

After putting out a July 2012 video outlining why the child star should date him, the pair began a long-distance relationship that lasted into 2013.

Following the breakup, Brooks took to X to accuse Grande of cheating on him with The Wanted’s Nathan Sykes, a claim she denied.

"I'm going to be the lady my mother raised and carry myself with class and dignity... But I will never be any man's press opportunity…” she wrote on X at the time. “It's always ok to defend yourself. My fans know what kind of person I am. Never let any man discredit u or the values you were raised with...I'm finally happy. Words can't hurt me anymore.”

Despite the back-and-forth, Grande and Brooks poured into their relationship one last time, reconciling in 2014, though they walked away from their connection for good months later.

After Grande and Sykes collaborated on their 2013 duet "Almost Is Never Enough,” Grande knew the boy was hers. Though the pair dated publicly for about five months, Grande told Brian Fink of Florida radio's 93.3 FLZ in December of that year that they’d broken up and remained “really good friends.”

In 2016, they teamed up yet again for their track “Over and Over Again.” And while there were some post-breakup jitters when it came to working together again, Sykes—who married wife Charlotte Burke in October 2025—detailed how he and the Wicked star quickly moved past any uncomfortable vibes.

"I spoke to [Ariana] and I was like, 'It's only as awkward as everyone else makes it,'" Sykes told Entertainment Tonight at the time. "If we don't make it awkward, then at the end of the day, after a couple of weeks, it's not going to be awkward anymore."

Romance rumors began about Grande and Big Sean—who had previously collaborated on tracks like “Best Mistake” and “Right There”—after they were spotted leaving a movie theater together in August 2014.

One month later, the “Blessings” rapper subtly confirmed their relationship.

"That Ariana is very, very special,” he said during his appearance on On Air with Ryan Seacrest in September 2014. “She's very special to me.”

And while the “thank u, next” hitmaker thought she’d end up with Sean, he wasn’t a match.

Grande and Sean—who welcomed son Noah with longtime partner Jhené Aiko in 2022—broke up in April 2015 after nearly nine months of dating due to conflicting tour schedules, a source previously told E! News.

In a joint statement, Grande and Sean’s reps shared they "care deeply for each other and remain close friends."

Mac Miller first teamed up with Grande professionally on a 2012 cover of “Baby It’s Cold Outside”—and later their 2013 single “The Way”—before their connection turned romantic.

Though they sparked dating rumors early on in their working relationship, Miller set the record straight after their steamy music video for the latter track raised eyebrows about the nature of their connection.

“That’s the homie. She’s got a boyfriend and everything,” Miller told MTV News in an April 2013 interview, referencing her romance with Brooks. “Obviously, that [kiss] made everyone talk. I didn’t even know that was going to happen and then we were shooting and the director was like, ‘This should happen,’ and I’m like, ‘Alright.’”

But it seems Miller was more game for the interaction than he let on. After all, the pair went public with their relationship in August 2016 while attending the MTV VMAs together.

Though they were able to collaborate on many more tracks together—including  “My Favorite Part” from Miller’s 2016 album The Divine Feminine—it was how they supported each other in the face of hardship that made their romance so strong.

After the terrorist bombing at Grande’s 2017 concert in Manchester—which claimed the lives of 22 people—Miller stood by her side, later joining her on stage at the benefit show she hosted to support the victims.

But in May 2018, Grande and Miller broke up.

“This is one of my best friends in the whole world and favorite people on the planet,” Grande wrote on Instagram Stories at the time. “I respect and adore him endlessly and am grateful to have him in my life in any form, at all times regardless of how our relationship changes or what the universe holds for each of us!”

Four months later, Miller tragically died following an accidental overdose. It wasn’t until a year later that Grande spoke publicly about her profound grief.

“It’s pretty all-consuming,” she told Vogue in a July 2019 interview. “By no means was what we had perfect, but, like, f--k. He was the best person ever, and he didn’t deserve the demons he had.”

“I was the glue for such a long time, and I found myself becoming less and less sticky,” she added. “The pieces just started to float away.”

Did Grande and Pete Davidson have the ultimate whirlwind romance? Yes, and?

The comedian made his relationship with the “Dangerous Woman” singer Instagram official in May 2018 after they met on Saturday Night Live.

Weeks later, Davidson debuted multiple tattoos in Grande’s honor before confirming his engagement to the “Into You” singer one month later.

“I feel like I won a contest, so sick,” Davidson said of the engagement during his June 2018 appearance on the Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon. “It’s f--king lit, Jimmy. It’s so lit.”

In August, the pair made their romance red carpet-official as they attended the 2018 MTV Video Music Awards together, just days after Grande dropped her fourth studio album Sweetener, which features the song “pete davidson.”

While they covered quite a bit of ground in their relationship together, Grande and Davidson—who has since welcomed a daughter Scottie Rose with ex Elsie Hewitt—broke up in October 2018, but not without Grande giving her former fiancé one last shoutout.

As Grande sings in “thank u, next,” “Even almost got married / And for Pete, I’m so thankful.”

And it wasn’t all that long after Grande’s split from Davidson that she found herself walking down the aisle holding hands with her mama.

She and Dalton Gomez began dating in the beginning of 2020, right before the COVID-19 pandemic put the pair on lockdown. The “yes, and?” singer and real estate agent quarantined together, making their love Instagram official that June.

And by December of that year, they imagined a world together as they got engaged.

Five months later, the pair tied the knot at their home in Montecito, California.

“They got married. It was tiny and intimate—less than 20 people,” Grande’s rep told People of the May 2021 nuptials. “The room was so happy and full of love. The couple and both families couldn’t be happier.”

But Grande and Gomez broke free from their marriage just two years later before settling the terms of their divorce in October 2023, according to documents obtained by E! News.

Per the agreement, according to TMZ, Gomez received a one-time tax-free payment of $1,250,000 and half the net proceeds of their L.A. home sale but did not collect spousal support.

Grande and Dalton finalized their divorce in March 2024.

Grande first discoverated her feelings for Ethan Slater on the set of Wicked before their romance began in July 2023. Two months later, they were seen on a Disney World date in photos obtained by TMZ.

A source close to Grande and Slater told E! News after the excursion, “they went with a big group of friends including her mom and brother and are really happy and really good for each other.”

And while the pair’s thrillifying romance got a stamp of approval from Grande’s brother Frankie Grande, who called him a “very sweet guy” in a June 2024 interview with TooFab, the couple’s relationship became the center of controversy following speculation there was overlap with their previous marriages.

“It definitely doesn’t get any easier, seeing some of the negativity that was birthed by disreputable tabloids,” Grande told Vanity Fair in 2024 of the chatter. “Of course, I went through a lot of life changes during the filming of this movie. A lot of people that were working on it did.”

Grande went on to defend Slater—who welcomed a son with ex-wife Lilly Jay in August 2022—against any negativity thrown at him.

“There couldn’t be a less accurate depiction of a human being than the one that the tabloids spread about him,” Grande added. “No one on this earth tries harder or spreads themselves thinner to be there for the people that he loves and cares about. There is no one on this earth with a better heart, and that is something that no bullshit tabloid can rewrite in real life.”

That same month, Slater finalized his divorce with Jay.

Following the changes in his personal life, the Broadway star opened up about the challenges of being catapulted into the spotlight.

“I think there was something that was really difficult about things in your private life being commented on and looked at by the public,” Slater told GQ in 2024. “There were a lot of big changes in private lives that were really happening, so it’s really hard to see people who don’t know anything about what’s happening commenting on it.”

While breakup rumors between the two began in late 2025, they called their three-year romance off for good in June 2026.

Grande and Ricky Álvarez’s love story began in 2015 after he joined the popstar on her Honeymoon Tour as a background dancer.

“We’re happy,” Grande told Billboard of her romance with Álvarez in a May 2016 interview. “I’m a very happy girl. I have a healthy life right now, and I think that’s all anyone cares to know. The end.”

Their romance proved to be short and sweet, with the musician and the professional dancer calling it quits just months later in July 2016.

But there were brighter days ahead for the couple, who were seen together during a June 2026 group lunch at De Nada Cantina in Austin.

One day later, Grande switched up the lyrics to her 2018 hit “thank u, next.” Though she usually followed the lyric, “Wrote some song about Ricky,” with, “now I listen and laugh,” at her Austin show she said, “They still really slap.”

Weeks later, she was back at it again, this time singing at her July 13 concert, “We always find our way back.”

Soon after, he found his way onto her grid, with Grande appearing to soft launch their romance on Instagram July 27 ahead of the release of her eighth album Petal.

As she captioned the post which included a clip of herself clinking olives with Álvarez, “petal season continued …….. !”

#802. Ukraine tries to shut Moscow's airports with drone strikes on Russia

Repeated Ukrainian drone attacks are increasingly disrupting operations at Moscow's airports. The pounding is part of Ukraine's plan to shut down Russia's airpace.

For months, drone strikes by Ukraine have forced the suspension of flights to and from airports in Russia. Moscow's Domodedovo, Sheremetyevo, Zhukovsky and Vnukovo airports have had to shut down operations almost daily in October, according to reports from the independent investigative media outlet Agentstvo. On some days, the airports were reportedly closed for up to nine hours.

In early September, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced that Ukraine would seek to cut off the airspace around Moscow and other destinations in Russia. "Today, we would like to warn every airline that uses Russian airspace, every insurer, and everyone who continues to use major Russian airports: Russian airspace will become completely unsafe," Zelenskyy said.

The following day, Ukraine sent a corresponding warning to the International Civil Aviation Organization.

Ukraine's airspace has been closed since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Russia's aviation authority, Rosaviatsiya, has issued an emergency safety "carpet" protocol that is designed to immediately shut down the airspace over a specific region or around affected airports if an aircraft violates Russian airspace, weapons are used, or unidentified objects appear in the skies. Once the protocol is announced, drastic restrictions apply to all air traffic.

"If there is a military threat, a specific section of airspace is closed off, and this carpet is declared," Oleksandr Laneckij, the chief executive officer of the Friendly Avia Support consultancy, told DW. "Essentially, every drone poses a military threat."

Laneckij noted that Yemen's Houthis have managed to significantly disrupt Saudi airspace. "I think Ukraine's military capabilities far exceed those of the Houthis," Laneckij said.

The military analyst Jan Matvejev also said Ukraine would have little trouble severely disrupting Moscow-area air traffic. Though Ukraine has not yet managed to completely shut down Russian airspace as Zelenskyy plans, Matvejev said, its armed forces "remain committed to this idea."

"To close off the airspace and trigger the 'carpet' plan, all you need are simple drones that don't have to be equipped with a warhead or even have a long range," Matvejev said. Ukraine's arms industry can produce hundreds of combat-ready long-range drones in a day, he added. That is why he believes Ukraine could have the necessary resources to shut down Moscow's airports.

Indeed, Ukraine's efforts to shut down Russian airspace are "just getting started," Simon Shuster wrote in October in the US magazine The Atlantic, citing well-informed sources.

Matvejev said Russia's air-defense systems were not entirely effective in efforts to prevent Ukrainian drones from penetrating Moscow's airspace. "If it were possible to shoot them down, they would have done so by now," he said. He added that Russia would have deployed additional air-defense troops if they were available.

Laneckij said Russia might lower the threshold for declaring the carpet protocol, which could increase the risk of deadly incidents such as the 2024 Christmas day crash of an Azerbaijan Airlines flight. Investigators say the flight was struck by a Russian air-defense missile that was being used to defend against drones, killing 38 people.

Matvejev seconded the fear that Russia's defenses could again mistakenly target civilian aircraft instead of military objects. He said little had changed about Russia's air-defense protocol since the Azeri flight was shot in 2024.

In an operation against a low-flying drone, the target is visually identified and fired upon with a machine gun. In such a scenario, the danger to aircraft is extremely low, unless they happen to be flying in the immediate vicinity.

The risk to civil aviation increases significantly when anti-aircraft missiles are deployed, Matvejev said. A missile could have defects that are practically unavoidable in mass production and could veer toward an aircraft flying nearby. Matvejev said such defense measures could not guarantee the safety of civilian aircraft during operations.

He said drones did not have to carry explosives to be disruptive. A collision between an airplane and a basic drone can have serious consequences — and, he said, a drone sent from Ukraine all the way to Moscow must be relatively large, "weighting dozens of kilograms."

In the summer of 2023, Ukrainian armed forces attacked the airport in the Russian city of Pskov, where both military and civilian aircraft were parked. Earlier this month, drone debris fell on the Sochi airport, on Russia's Black Sea coast.

Russia also attacks Ukraine's airports. In September, Zelenskyy said Kyiv's airport had been struck, as well as the Boryspil airport near the capital.

Laneckij said three factors would determine whether international airlines suspend their flights to Russia: the military threat, the degree of demand and the insurance cost.

He said issues could emerge around insurance. When insurers rate the security risk of flying to Russia as very high, they could significantly raise their rates for aircraft headed there. This would cause ticket prices to skyrocket.

Competition within Russia's aviation market has already declined because many airlines are no longer in business, Laneckij said. This has increased demand for tickets from the remaining foreign airlines.

"Whether they stay or not depends on the price they have to pay for the danger faced," he said.

#799. No Grealish, no problem - the rise of Everton's youngsters

Players aged 24 or under are playing a higher proportion of minutes for Everton this season

As Everton prepared to face Newcastle in the fourth round of the EFL Cup at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday, the stakes were high.

A quarter-final tie against League Two opposition in Fleetwood awaited the winner, and a fanbase starved of trophies began to look ahead - albeit, for some, through covered eyes.

Then, in the build-up to the match, it was revealed Jack Grealish had been dropped from the squad over what is understood to have been an unauthorised absence from training.

The unwanted headline threatened to derail preparations for the latest round of a competition that perhaps offers Everton's best chance of winning a trophy for the first time in 31 years.

Instead, the club's younger players came to the fore, led by the influential Hayden Hackney.

A Â£16.5m summer signing from Middlesbrough, the 24-year-old made light of his inexperience at the highest level against a strong Newcastle XI, assisting James Garner's opening goal before scoring Everton's second with a close-range volley.

Hackney, though, has needed to be patient early in his Everton career.

After starting the opening game of the season - a 2-0 win against Crystal Palace - his only subsequent start prior to Thursday's cup victory was in the third round of the same competition against Wolves.

The central midfielder is not known for being prolific - the fourth-round win was only the second time in his career he had scored and assisted in the same game - but he knitted together phases of possession and carried the ball with the confidence that led to him being named Championship player of the year last season.

David Moyes, though, is a demanding manager and one perfectly prepared to keep young feet on the ground.

"I thought there were bits of his game that were very good," said the Everton boss. "Getting a goal was great. There were other bits where I didn't think it was where it was [supposed to be].

"But I see this as a bit of bringing in Championship players, getting them used to the Premier League. A couple of times he got caught on the ball.

"But I really enjoyed bits. He gave us a bit of an attacking play, getting into the box, and obviously getting the goal was really good. A really good assist from Thierno Barry as well, to be fair."

While Hackney was ably assisted by strong performances from Garner and Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall in Everton's midfield, the threadbare nature of the Toffees' squad means the development and contribution of the club's younger players could prove crucial in any success this season.

Of the 10 players signed on permanent deals since Moyes rejoined the club in January 2025, seven are aged 24 or under, including Barry.

The France Under-21 international is playing just a third season in a top-five European league after joining from Villarreal in July 2025, but his introduction to elite football has been more pressurised because of Everton's lack of options up front.

Barry is the club's only specialist centre-forward, starting every match and playing 918 minutes this season. His tally of seven goals is already just one off his total from last season, despite playing 30 fewer matches.

Everton have recorded 24 big chances, and Barry has been involved in 15 of them (62.5%).

Whiles Moyes' hand has been somewhat forced in giving Barry game time because of a lack of alternatives, there has been a broader indication he is more prepared to back the younger members of his squad this season.

The average age of Everton's starting XI in the Premier League has dropped by almost 18 months this season to 26 years and 216 days.

The departure of veteran midfielder Idrissa Gueye has made a difference but first-team players aged 24 or under are playing a much higher proportion of Premier League minutes than in the previous campaign.

Moyes used just 22 players in the Premier League last season. He has already used 22 in this one.

Even the youngest players in the squad appear to have gained more trust. In 2025-26, players aged 21 or under totalled 1,088 minutes for the Toffees, a figure that has already been exceeded this season (1,206).

At 19, Harrison Armstrong is the youngest regular in Everton's senior squad. In January, he had completed a six-month loan spell at Preston and Moyes considered sending him back to Deepdale for the remainder of last season before slowly integrating him into the first team.

This season, the teenager has started every Premier League match.

Winger Tyler Dibling, 20, initially struggled after a Â£35m move from Southampton in the summer of 2025 but was positive in getting Everton on to the front foot on against Newcastle on Thursday night.

Tyrique George joined on a permanent deal from Chelsea in the summer after spending the second half of last season on loan at Everton during which he made only one league start.

The 20-year-old has already made five this season, scoring his first goal for the club in the 2-2 draw with Manchester United in September.

George also started the EFL Cup fixture last week and won back possession for the opening goal.

Merlin Rohl broke into the team towards the end of last season and the 24-year-old midfielder, who also signed permanently in the summer following an initial loan spell, has since been trusted to fill Everton's problem position of right-back.

After missing four games because of injury, he was immediately brought back into the starting XI against Chelsea. He was then preferred to the more experienced Ainsley Maitland-Niles at right-back for matches against Arsenal and Newcastle.

When asked if Grealish would return to the squad for Monday's rematch at St James' Park, Moyes said he would not reveal any team news, though there is no doubt that experience still counts among the 63-year-old's most valuable commodities.

Defender James Tarkowksi, 33, has been a standout performer so far this season, while the form of fellow senior players such as Jordan Pickford, 32, and Dewsbury-Hall, 28 remain critical to this Everton side.

But when Everton meet Newcastle for the second time in less than a week on Monday, Grealish could again miss out.

In his absence, younger heads were good enough to win a cup tie. It would be further indication of their growing influence if they were to repeat that result in the Premier League.

#798. Tearful Ellen DeGeneres Honors Producer Matthew Wright After His Death

Ellen DeGeneres honored Ellen Show producer Matthew Wright days after his sudden death at age 52: “Everyone loved him. I loved him, and it's just shocking.”

Ellen DeGeneres is remembering an unforgettable member of her eponymous talk show’s team.

Days after the family of The Ellen DeGeneres Show's executive producer Matthew Wright confirmed in a GoFundMe that he had died at 52 in an “unfathomable tragedy," the Emmy winner expressed her grief over the news.

“Hi, everybody,” DeGeneres said in a video shared to Instagram Nov. 2. “So, Matt Wright, who was our executive producer and was featured on our show a lot, died the other day. And he was an amazing guy. He was funny. God, he made me laugh.”

“He would surprise me with things that he did all the time,” she continued while holding back tears. “He was smart and he was kind. He was a part of our show. I mean, everyone loved him. I loved him, and it's just shocking.”

And the loss was even more difficult to process considering she and Wright were working together on a project at the time of his untimely death. And while it’s true Wright and DeGeneres were a dream team professionally, the 68-year-old shared their relationship went much deeper.

“We're gonna miss him,” she said. “He is, and always will be, the glue to our entire family at the Ellen Show.”

“And to Justin, his husband,” she continued, “and to his family, I'm so sorry, because we lost a good guy. He was a good guy.”

The comedian also detailed his tight bond with Ellen co-executive producer and DJ Stephen "tWitch" Boss, who tragically died by suicide in 2022.

“He and tWitch were so close,” she said. “So now he and tWitch are together, dancing and laughing.”

But DeGeneres wasn’t the only member of the show’s team to speak out about Wright’s passing. In fact, Andy Lassner, who also worked as an EP on Ellen, shared he was with his former colleague just “hours” before he died.

Wright had come to visit Lassner on the set of The Jennifer Hudson Show’s Halloween episode. But hours later, “he was gone.”

“We are all in shock,” Lassner wrote on Instagram Nov. 1. “He was a brilliant producer and an even better human being. The way he looked after his mom, flying back and forth from Los Angeles to New York practically every weekend before she died, showed what an incredible son he was.”

Wright worked on Ellen for 16 years. And when the talk show ended in 2022, he shared how proud he was that the show would be a lasting chapter in his story.

“How do I even begin to sum up 16 years of my life? I’ve made so many best friends, had so many amazing experiences, met so many heroes of mine and even fell in love thanks to this show,” he wrote. “I will forever be grateful to @theellenshow for taking a chance on me and changing my life! Here’s to an amazing run!”

#797. Falkirk brick wall Bain boosts Scotland chances

Falkirk goalkeeper Scott Bain produced an outstanding performance in the 2-0 win over Celtic

Scott Bain must be praying that Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli was watching on as Falkirk ended a 19-year wait to beat Celtic.

The former Celtic goalkeeper was imperious, unbeatable, as Falkirk ran out 2-0 winners to earn a fourth win on the bounce and reach fourth place in the Scottish Premiership.

An absolute brick wall as he earned a third clean sheet in a row.

Not that all the praise should go his way. Everyone in Bairns blue delivered, but Bain was inspired, making save after save to deny Celtic on a day that will go down in Falkirk folklore. One that intensified the pressure on Martin O'Neill's side.

With the Scotland squad for the upcoming Nations League fixtures announced this week, surely Bain has enhanced his chances of pushing for not just a place in the squad but potentially the chance to stake a claim for a starting role.

Listen: Derby delight for Hibs, fresh questions for Celtic

Are Celtic club in regression amid run of six defeats in 10?

Impressive Falkirk earn first win over hapless Celtic in 19 years

Bain made nine saves against Celtic, with a number of them outstanding, as his side kept a clean sheet for the third game in a row.

That's now a run of 342 minutes without conceding a goal for the Bairns.

"Scott Bain was unbelievable," former Celtic goalkeeper Pat Bonner enthused. "Absolutely unbelievable.

"It was a terrific display from Falkirk defensively. Falkirk deserve it. They've got a terrific young team."

Bain himself explained how he felt as he zoned in on repelling Celtic no matter what they threw at him.

"I felt really confident in the game," he said. "I felt confident in the players and the game plan and I knew that I would be called upon, but it just felt like one of those days where they weren't going to score.

"You can't really get a better day as a goalkeeper than thinking that you're not going to be beaten. So, really, really pleased for my own performance, but more so pleased for the team. It's a fantastic step in the right direction."

The Scotland international extended his Falkirk contract in January and is tied to the club until the summer of 2028, with the option of a further year.

At the time, manager John McGlynn stated that "he's been outstanding from the moment he walked into the club".

After this fabulous display, he lavished even more praise on his number one, who turns 35 this month.

"Scott Bain had two really outstanding saves [in the first half] and there might have been another very good save, but there weren't as many as there were in the second half where he had to continuously produce," he said.

"So a huge thank you to Scott for the actual game he's had today."

No talk of that just being his job but genuine thanks for a memorable afternoon that went a long way to delivering a memorable win.

Bain took a step out of his comfort zone as back-up at Celtic. A sizeable drop in salary to pursue his ambition of regular game time. Days like this surely make that decision justified.

With Scotland lacking the sort of goalkeeping depth they enjoyed for so many years, displays like this can certainly do no harm.

There's an argument that Bain, outside of his shot-stopping ability that was on full display against Celtic, has the type of composure with his feet that may suit Pocognoli's approach.

"I think I've performed well since the last camp and I think I've been performing well throughout the season," Bain added.

"So I would hope to be in it [Scotland squad]. I really enjoyed the last camp. I really enjoyed the way the manager worked and seeing what he wants from his team.

"I'd be delighted if I can get back in and experience more time with him."

This time, the four-time capped goalkeeper may have enhanced his chances of adding to that tally.

Janelle Brown was as shocked as Sister Wives fans to learn this news.

Less than a month after season 21 of the TLC series kicked off without Janelle’s ex Kody Brown and his only remaining wife Robyn Brown, Janelle shared it was just as unexpected from the inside out.

Okay,’” she told People in an interview published on Nov. 2. “I haven’t talked to them since, well, since we were all together after we sold the property and I don’t know anything about what’s going on in their lives. And so yeah, I’m like, ‘Okay, I guess this is what we’re doing now.’”

While surprising, Janelle—who welcomed six kids with Kody before their December 2022 separation—sees the positive in Kody and Robyn’s departure. To her, it’s an opportunity for herself and Kody’s other exes Christine Brown and Meri Brown to turn the page.

Hunting Wives' Brittany Snow made a rare comment about her 2023 divorce from Selling The OC's Tyler Stanaland, which she said she was “grateful” for.

Brittany Snow's outlook on her divorce is pitch perfect.

The Hunting Wives actress made a rare comment about her divorce from Selling The OC star Tyler Stanaland, who she married in 2020 before separating two years later.

"I am so grateful that I went through that because the person that I am and the partner I’m with now, it’s just so different,” Snow said during the Nov. 2 episode of the Armchair Expert podcast. “I can’t believe I’m grateful for my divorce."

She continued, "I was 37 and I was living in an Airbnb, just staring at my dog being like, 'I don’t know what’s going to happen. It’s just you and me, kiddo. We’re going to try to rebuild this.'"

Snow—who finalized her divorce from Stanaland in 2023—found solace in other women online who were sharing stories that were similar to what she was going through at the time.

"I really appreciated so many women, friends of mine that were like, ‘That happened to me,'" she recalled. "I would go on Reddit and look up stories from women going through things in their later 30s, and finding people later in life. We have to make it what we make of it."

#794. Mighty Ducks’ Shaun Weiss Details 7-Year Sobriety Journey

Mighty Ducks’ alum Shaun Weiss opened up in an exclusive E! News interview about his seven-year journey with sobriety and his struggles with addiction and homelessness. “I really suffered,” he said.

Shaun Weiss had more than one slip on the ice before he got to where he is today.

The Mighty Ducks star recently shared insight into his latest sobriety milestone, detailing the difficult journey it took to get there.

“I've been clean for seven years,” Weiss told E! News in an exclusive interview. “I lived in sober living for three years. I did inpatient treatment for a whole year.”

And now that he’s skating down a steadier path, the former child star is taking what he’s learned and paying it forward, working to launch charities in Los Angeles and Atlanta that give those experiencing addiction and homelessness an opportunity to get clean in a safe, healthy environment.

"I've seen literally hundreds of young addicts come and go,” he explained.  I've seen what works. I've seen what doesn't work. The only way that I was really able to get clean was that I had access to really high-end level treatment.”

So, being able to help others struggling is what fulfills him. As he put it, “I’m really excited about that and that’s where I find my purpose.”

Meanwhile, with so many years of sobriety behind him, Weiss can see what personal problems led to his struggles with addiction.

“I know in my personal case, I was just never really a happy guy,” he recalled. “I was always reaching for things on the outside to fill me up. It wasn’t until really I found yoga and started doing some yogic practices and learned to be self-contained—just be more being more in control of my own happiness.”

When it came to his struggles with depression, the Pee-Wee’s Playhouse alum acknowledged, “That's the fundamental jump off point of the problems that lead to drugs.”

The 48-year-old also considered that his role as a child actor didn’t help keep him out of trouble.

“The lines get crossed and it can get to a level where it's unmanageable,” he shared. “It was really hard for my parents to discipline me when I was making the car payments.”

But while Weiss—who recently dived back into acting by starring as Freddy in Deformelody: An American Nightmare last year—has been dealt his fair share of struggles, he wouldn’t turn in any of his cards.

“I don't have any regrets,” he said. “I've had sort of a life that's been tumultuous at times, but I'm really happy with the guy I am today, and I don't think I'd be that guy if I hadn't suffered through all those experiences.”

If the Heavyweights actor could share one thing with his younger self, though? He posited, “I’d probably just say, ‘Hang in there. Everything will be alright.’”

And it had no effect on his success. "It wasn't like I was stumbling around all day," he admitted. "I was fully functioning — I wrote more songs then than I do now. That was the scary part."

In late 2011, he was hospitalized with pancreatitis and was told that if he didn't stop drinking, he wouldn't see his next birthday. "I still put it off and was trying to slow down on my own, like, 'All right I'm only gonna let myself take two pills today. I'm only gonna drink this much of my bottle and make a mark on the bottle,'" he recalled. "And it would work a couple days—and then somebody throws a party."

He eventually sought help, entering rehab on Dec. 18, 2011. "I got to the point where I knew it was something I couldn't do on my own," Gilbert said. "Pissed me off to no end and embarrassed me. I'm a pretty strong-willed person but that was the one thing in my life that I couldn't get to stick."
